1	# Getting Started — For Teammates
2	
3	Welcome to PC Pal! This guide will get you up and running in 5 minutes.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## What is this project?
8	
9	PC Pal is a web app that helps elderly people learn to use their computer. Users chat with an AI assistant that:
10	- Explains things in simple language
11	- Shows visual guide cards with numbered steps and keyboard diagrams
12	- Tracks what skills they've learned
13	- Detects emergencies and scams
14	
15	**You don't need an API key to run it.** The app has a built-in demo mode.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## Quick Start
20	
21	### 1. Clone & Install
22	
23	```bash
24	git clone https://github.com/your-org/COS498-Group-7-Repo.git
25	cd COS498-Group-7-Repo
26	npm install
27	cd client && npm install && cd ..
28	```
29	
30	### 2. Create your .env file
31	
32	```bash
33	cp .env.example .env
34	```
35	
36	That's it. The defaults enable demo mode automatically.
37	
38	### 3. Start the app
39	
40	```bash
41	npm run dev
42	```
43	
44	This starts two servers:
45	- **Backend** on http://localhost:3001
46	- **Frontend** on http://localhost:5173
47	
48	### 4. Open in your browser
49	
50	Go to **http://localhost:5173**
51	
52	You'll see the onboarding wizard. Fill in a name, pick a device, set comfort level, and you're in the chat.
53	
54	---
55	
56	## Try These in Demo Mode
57	
58	| Type this | What happens |
59	|-----------|-------------|
60	| "How do I copy and paste?" | Visual guide card appears + step-by-step walkthrough starts |
61	| "done" or "next" | Advances to the next step |
62	| "How do I take a screenshot?" | Another visual guide with keyboard shortcuts |
63	| "What should I learn next?" | Suggests the next skill based on your progress |
64	| "My notes" | Shows saved tips from your session |
65	| "Start over" | Clears the conversation |
66	| "Help" | Lists everything PC Pal can help with |
67	| "I've fallen" | Triggers the emergency alert system |
68	
69	---
70	
71	## Project Structure (High Level)
72	
73	```
74	client/           React frontend (what the user sees)
75	server/           Node.js backend (the brains)
76	  core/           Business logic (AI agent, safety, vocabulary)
77	  models/         Database access (users, messages, skills)
78	  routes/         REST API endpoints
79	  db/             SQLite database
80	docs/             Documentation (you are here)
81	```
82	
83	**Want more detail?** Read `docs/file-by-file-guide.md` for a breakdown of every file.
84	
85	**Want the big picture?** Read `docs/architecture-overview.md` for how everything connects.
86	
87	---
88	
89	## Common Tasks
90	
91	### Run tests
92	```bash
93	npm test
94	```
95	74 tests, takes about 1 second.
96	
97	### Reset the database
98	Delete `server/db/pcpal.db` and restart the server. A fresh database is created automatically.
99	
100	### Switch from demo mode to real AI
101	1. Get an API key from [console.anthropic.com](https://console.anthropic.com/)
102	2. Edit `.env`:
103	   ```
104	   REDACTED
105	   MOCK_MODE=false
106	   ```
107	3. Restart the server
108	
109	### Add a new visual guide
110	1. Open `client/src/components/Chat/guideRegistry.js`
111	2. Add a new entry following the existing pattern (title, Windows/Mac steps, optional keyboard keys)
112	3. Add the new ID to `VALID_GUIDE_IDS` in `server/core/agentOrchestrator.js`
113	
114	### Add a new vocabulary substitution
115	1. Open `server/assets/vocabulary/basicSubstitutions.json`
116	2. Add a new `"technical_term": "simple replacement"` entry
117	
118	---
119	
120	## Tech Stack Summary

# Getting Started — For Teammates

Welcome to PC Pal! This guide will get you up and running in 5 minutes.

---

## What is this project?

PC Pal is a web app that helps elderly people learn to use their computer. Users chat with an AI assistant that:
- Explains things in simple language
- Shows visual guide cards with numbered steps and keyboard diagrams
- Tracks what skills they've learned
- Detects emergencies and scams

**You don't need an API key to run it.** The app has a built-in demo mode.

---

## Quick Start

### 1. Clone & Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/COS498-Group-7-Repo.git
cd COS498-Group-7-Repo
npm install
cd client && npm install && cd ..
```

### 2. Create your .env file

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

That's it. The defaults enable demo mode automatically.

### 3. Start the app

```bash
npm run dev
```

This starts two servers:
- **Backend** on http://localhost:3001
- **Frontend** on http://localhost:5173

### 4. Open in your browser

Go to **http://localhost:5173**

You'll see the onboarding wizard. Fill in a name, pick a device, set comfort level, and you're in the chat.

---

## Try These in Demo Mode

| Type this | What happens |
|-----------|-------------|
| "How do I copy and paste?" | Visual guide card appears + step-by-step walkthrough starts |
| "done" or "next" | Advances to the next step |
| "How do I take a screenshot?" | Another visual guide with keyboard shortcuts |
| "What should I learn next?" | Suggests the next skill based on your progress |
| "My notes" | Shows saved tips from your session |
| "Start over" | Clears the conversation |
| "Help" | Lists everything PC Pal can help with |
| "I've fallen" | Triggers the emergency alert system |

---

## Project Structure (High Level)

```
client/           React frontend (what the user sees)
server/           Node.js backend (the brains)
  core/           Business logic (AI agent, safety, vocabulary)
  models/         Database access (users, messages, skills)
  routes/         REST API endpoints
  db/             SQLite database
docs/             Documentation (you are here)
```

**Want more detail?** Read `docs/file-by-file-guide.md` for a breakdown of every file.

**Want the big picture?** Read `docs/architecture-overview.md` for how everything connects.

---

## Common Tasks

### Run tests
```bash
npm test
```
74 tests, takes about 1 second.

### Reset the database
Delete `server/db/pcpal.db` and restart the server. A fresh database is created automatically.

### Switch from demo mode to real AI
1. Get an API key from [console.anthropic.com](https://console.anthropic.com/)
2. Edit `.env`:
   ```
   REDACTED
   MOCK_MODE=false
   ```
3. Restart the server

### Add a new visual guide
1. Open `client/src/components/Chat/guideRegistry.js`
2. Add a new entry following the existing pattern (title, Windows/Mac steps, optional keyboard keys)
3. Add the new ID to `VALID_GUIDE_IDS` in `server/core/agentOrchestrator.js`

### Add a new vocabulary substitution
1. Open `server/assets/vocabulary/basicSubstitutions.json`
2. Add a new `"technical_term": "simple replacement"` entry

---

## Tech Stack Summary

| What | Technology | Why |
|------|-----------|-----|
| Frontend | React + Vite | Fast dev server, component-based UI |
| Backend | Node.js + Express | JavaScript everywhere, good WebSocket support |
| Real-time | WebSocket (`ws`) | Typing indicators, instant responses |
| AI | Claude API (Anthropic) | Best at tool-use and following instructions |
| Database | SQLite | Zero setup, single file, good enough for prototype |
| Tests | Jest | Standard Node.js test runner |

---

## Who Built What

This is the first prototype. The core implementation includes:
- 12 AI agent tools
- 10 visual task guides (Windows + Mac)
- Safety monitoring (emergencies + scams)
- Vocabulary simplification (20+ terms)
- Comfort-level adaptive responses
- Full demo mode
- 74 automated tests

---

## Need Help?

- **Architecture questions** → `docs/architecture-overview.md`
- **"What does this file do?"** → `docs/file-by-file-guide.md`
- **Setup problems** → Check that Node.js v18+ is installed and both `npm install` commands ran
- **Database issues** → Delete `server/db/pcpal.db` and restart

302	   - Display in VisualGuide.jsx component in chat
303	   - Files: server/core/visualGuideGenerator.js, server/assets/screenshots/, client/src/components/Chat/VisualGuide.jsx
304	 5. Skill tracker
305	   - logSkill(userId, skillName, status) — write to skill_events
306	   - getUserSkills(userId) — list all learned skills
307	   - getSkillsForReinforcement(userId) — skills not practiced in 7+ days
308	   - File: server/core/skillTracker.js

327

329	
330	 1. Scaffolding fade logic
331	   - If user completed a skill 3+ times, agent offers: "Want to try this on your own first?"
332	   - On success: positive reinforcement. On failure: resume guided mode
333	   - Update: server/core/agentOrchestrator.js, server/core/skillTracker.js
334	 2. Accessibility improvements
335	   - Theme toggle: high contrast / large text / default
336	   - Keyboard navigation throughout
337	   - Larger step counts (more granular) for users with accessibility needs
338	   - Update: client/src/styles/globals.css, client/src/components/
339	 3. Skill history sidebar
340	   - Sidebar.jsx — shows all learned skills with dates and practice count
341	   - GET /api/users/:id/skills endpoint
342	   - Files: client/src/components/Layout/Sidebar.jsx, server/routes/skills.js
343	 4. Proactive messages (in-app)
344	   - node-cron job checks for skill reinforcement opportunities
345	   - Sends in-app notification: "Want to practice [skill] today?"
346	   - File: server/core/proactiveEngine.js
347	 5. Deployment
348	   - Build React → static files served by Express
349	   - Deploy to Railway or Render
350	   - Environment variables for secrets
351	   - Update: server/index.js (serve static), README.md
352	 6. Evaluation prep
353	   - Pre/post confidence survey component in React
354	   - Conversation log export endpoint: GET /api/conversations/:id/export
355	   - Skill completion rate metrics
356	
357	 ---
358	 Key Design Decisions
359	
360	 WebSocket for real-time chat: Streaming Claude responses token-by-token gives a natural chat feel. Fallback REST endpoint for
361	 reliability.
362	
363	 SQLite for v1/v2: Zero setup, single file DB. Same query patterns transfer to PostgreSQL for production. better-sqlite3 is synchronous    
364	 but fast enough for a class project. If async needed, switch to sqlite3 with promises.
365	
366	 Elderly-friendly UI defaults: 18px+ base font, high-contrast colors, large buttons, minimal navigation. No complex UI patterns — just a   
367	 chat window and onboarding wizard.
368	
369	 Context compression at 20 messages: Bounds token cost while maintaining conversation continuity. Claude summarizes older messages into a  
370	 compact context string.
371	
372	 Tool-use agent loop: Claude decides when to use tools (create steps, log skills, flag emergencies) rather than hardcoded routing. More    
373	 flexible and natural conversation flow.
374	
375	 ---
376	 Verification Plan
377	
378	 Local dev
379	
380	 1. npm install in root and client/
381	 2. Set .env with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
382	 3. npm run dev — starts Express (port 3001) + Vite dev server (port 5173) with proxy
383	 4. Open http://localhost:5173 in browser
384	
385	 Automated tests
386	
387	 - npm test — Jest tests for backend modules
388	 - Mock Claude API responses with Jest mocks
389	 - React Testing Library for component tests
390	
391	 Manual QA checklist per version
392	
393	 - Onboarding wizard collects name + OS + comfort level
394	 - Chat message sends and receives response
395	 - Vocabulary simplification in responses
396	 - Emergency keyword triggers safety alert
397	 - (v2) Step-by-step flow with progress bar and confirmation
398	 - (v2) Annotated screenshot displays in chat
399	 - (v2) Scam detection warning displays
400	 - (v3) Skill fade ("try on your own") after 3 completions
401	 - (v3) Skill history sidebar shows learned skills
402	 - (v3) Deployed and accessible via public URL

 Delivery: Web UI (React) first. SMS (Twilio) and CollaborAITE integration planned for later.

 Timeline: v1 by Apr 14 | v2 by Apr 21 | v3 by Apr 28

 ---
 Tech Stack

 ┌──────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │    Component     │                        Choice                        │
 ├──────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Frontend         │ React (Vite)                                         │
 ├──────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Backend          │ Node.js + Express                                    │
 ├──────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ AI               │ Anthropic SDK (@anthropic-ai/sdk) with tool-use      │
 ├──────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Database         │ SQLite (v1/v2 via better-sqlite3), PostgreSQL for v3 │
 ├──────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Real-time        │ WebSocket (via ws or Socket.IO) for streaming chat   │
 ├──────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Image Processing │ Sharp (Node.js) for annotated screenshots (v2)       │
 ├──────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Scheduling       │ node-cron (v2+ for proactive messages)               │
 ├──────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Testing          │ Jest (backend), React Testing Library (frontend)     │
 └──────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

 ---
 Architecture - Message Flow

 React Chat UI (browser)
     |  WebSocket or POST /api/chat
     v
 Express Server (server/index.js)
     |
     v
 ConversationRouter (server/core/conversationRouter.js)
     |  lookup user, load/create session
     v
 SafetyMonitor (runs FIRST on every message)
     |  emergency/scam detection
     v
 TaskClassifier (Claude call)
     |  learn_skill | troubleshoot | follow_up | accessibility
     v
 AgentOrchestrator (Claude tool-use loop)
     |  system prompt with user profile, history, vocab level
     |  tools: get_next_step, complete_step, log_skill, flag_emergency
     v
 VocabularyFilter
     |  replace jargon, enforce sentence length
     v
 WebSocket/Response  →  React Chat UI

 ---
 Project Structure

 client/                          # React frontend (Vite)
   src/
     App.jsx                      # Main app with routing
     components/
       Chat/
         ChatWindow.jsx           # Main chat container
         MessageBubble.jsx        # Individual message display
         MessageInput.jsx         # Text input + send button
         StepIndicator.jsx        # "Step 2 of 5" progress bar
         VisualGuide.jsx          # Annotated screenshot display (v2)

       Layout/

         Sidebar.jsx              # Skill history panel (v3)
     hooks/

       globals.css                # Large fonts, high contrast, elderly-friendly
     main.jsx

     Conversation.js              # Conversation CRUD

   core/
     agentOrchestrator.js         # Claude tool-use agent loop
     taskClassifier.js            # Message classification via Claude

     vocabularyFilter.js          # Jargon replacement + readability
     skillTracker.js              # Skill logging + reinforcement
     safetyMonitor.js             # Emergency + scam detection

 package.json
 .env.example
 README.md

 ---
 Database Schema (SQLite)

 users

 CREATE TABLE users (
   id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,            -- UUID
   name TEXT,
   os_type TEXT,                   -- 'Windows 10', 'Windows 11', 'macOS', 'iPhone', 'Android'
   vocabulary_level TEXT DEFAULT 'basic',  -- basic | intermediate | standard
   accessibility_needs TEXT DEFAULT '[]',  -- JSON array
   comfort_level INTEGER DEFAULT 1,       -- 1-5
   onboarded INTEGER DEFAULT 0,           -- boolean
   created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
   updated_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
 );

 conversations

 CREATE TABLE conversations (
   id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
   user_id TEXT REFERENCES users(id),
   task_type TEXT,
   status TEXT DEFAULT 'active',          -- active | completed | abandoned
   context_summary TEXT,                  -- compressed older context
   started_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
   ended_at TEXT
 );

 messages

 CREATE TABLE messages (
   id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
   conversation_id TEXT REFERENCES conversations(id),
   role TEXT NOT NULL,                     -- 'user' | 'assistant'
   body TEXT NOT NULL,
   created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
 );

 step_sequences

 CREATE TABLE step_sequences (
   id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
   conversation_id TEXT REFERENCES conversations(id),
   steps TEXT NOT NULL,                   -- JSON array of step objects
   current_index INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
   completed INTEGER DEFAULT 0
 );

 skill_events

 CREATE TABLE skill_events (
   id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
   user_id TEXT REFERENCES users(id),
   skill_name TEXT NOT NULL,
   status TEXT DEFAULT 'started',         -- started | completed | abandoned
   practiced_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
 );

 safety_events

 CREATE TABLE safety_events (
   id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
   user_id TEXT REFERENCES users(id),
   event_type TEXT NOT NULL,              -- emergency | scam_detected | distress
   trigger_text TEXT,
   created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
 );

 ---
 Implementation Phases

 Phase 1 — v1 by April 14 (Core Chat Loop)

 Goal: User opens the web app, onboards (name + OS), and gets context-aware IT help from Claude with simplified vocabulary through a chat  
 interface.

 Steps:

 1. Project setup
   - Initialize Node.js project with package.json
   - Initialize React project with Vite in client/
   - Create .env.example with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
   - Create server/config.js for env loading
   - Create server/db/database.js + schema.sql with all tables
   - Files: package.json, .env.example, server/config.js, server/db/*
 2. Express server + WebSocket
   - Express app in server/index.js with CORS, JSON parsing
   - WebSocket server (ws library) on same port for real-time chat
   - On WS connection: assign/lookup user session
   - On WS message: route through processing pipeline, send response back
   - REST fallback: POST /api/chat for non-WebSocket clients
   - File: server/index.js, server/routes/chat.js
 3. React chat UI
   - ChatWindow.jsx — scrollable message list + input
   - MessageBubble.jsx — styled differently for user vs assistant messages
   - MessageInput.jsx — large text input, prominent send button
   - useChat.js hook — manages WebSocket connection, message state, send/receive
   - Elderly-friendly CSS: minimum 18px font, high contrast, large click targets, simple layout
   - Files: client/src/components/Chat/*, client/src/hooks/useChat.js, client/src/styles/globals.css
 4. Onboarding flow
   - OnboardingFlow.jsx — large-button wizard: "What's your name?", "What computer do you use?" (Windows/Mac/iPhone/Android with icons),   
 "How comfortable are you with computers?" (1-5 scale)
   - Saves to users table via POST /api/users
   - Shown on first visit, skipped after (user ID stored in localStorage)
   - Files: client/src/components/Onboarding/OnboardingFlow.jsx, server/routes/users.js
 5. User profile manager
   - getOrCreateUser(id), updateProfile(id, fields)
   - Returns full user profile for system prompt injection
   - File: server/core/userProfileManager.js, server/models/User.js
 6. Task classifier
   - Single Claude call with classification prompt
   - Returns: learn_skill | troubleshoot | follow_up | accessibility | unknown
   - Also extracts: topic, urgency
   - File: server/core/taskClassifier.js
 7. Agent orchestrator
   - Build system prompt from user profile (name, OS, vocab level, skill history)
   - Claude messages API with tool-use: log_skill_started, flag_emergency
   - Load last 20 messages from DB as conversation history
   - Patient, elderly-appropriate tone in system prompt
   - Stream responses via WebSocket for real-time feel
   - File: server/core/agentOrchestrator.js
 8. Vocabulary filter
   - JSON config with word substitutions (browser→internet, attachment→file in the email, etc.)
   - filterResponse(text, vocabLevel) — applies substitutions
   - Sentence length enforcement: split sentences > 20 words
   - File: server/core/vocabularyFilter.js, server/assets/vocabulary/basicSubstitutions.json
 9. Conversation state
   - getOrCreateSession(userId) — find active session or start new
   - closeSession(sessionId) — mark completed
   - Timeout: abandon sessions inactive > 30 min
   - File: server/core/conversationState.js, server/models/Conversation.js
 10. Safety monitor (basic)
   - Emergency keyword regex: "fallen", "can't breathe", "chest pain", "help me", "911", "emergency"
   - On match: immediate response + log to safety_events
   - Display alert banner in chat UI
   - File: server/core/safetyMonitor.js
 11. Basic tests
   - Test vocabulary filter substitutions
   - Test safety monitor keyword detection
   - Test task classifier with mocked Claude responses
   - Files: server/__tests__/vocabularyFilter.test.js, server/__tests__/safetyMonitor.test.js

 ---
 Phase 2 — v2 by April 21 (Step Sequencer + Visual Guides + Skill Tracking)

 Goal: Multi-turn step-by-step walkthroughs with annotated screenshots displayed in chat.

 Steps:

 1. Step sequencer
   - createSequence(task, userId) — Claude generates numbered steps, stored in step_sequences
   - getCurrentStep(sessionId) — returns step text + "Step X of Y"
   - advanceStep(sessionId) — on user confirmation ("ok", "done", "got it", "next", "yes")
   - isConfirmation(text) — fuzzy match for elderly-friendly confirmations
   - File: server/core/stepSequencer.js
 2. Step UI component
   - StepIndicator.jsx — progress bar showing "Step 2 of 5"
   - Quick-reply buttons: "OK, done!", "I need help", "Go back"
   - File: client/src/components/Chat/StepIndicator.jsx
 3. Agent orchestrator v2 — add tool-use for steps
   - New tools: create_step_sequence, get_current_step, advance_step, send_visual_guide
   - Agent decides when to break a task into steps vs. quick answer
   - Update: server/core/agentOrchestrator.js
 4. Visual guide generator
   - Pre-captured base screenshots for top 10 tasks (Windows 10/11, macOS)
   - Sharp overlay: red circles, arrows, numbered callouts at JSON-defined coordinates
   - Serve annotated images via Express static route /assets/guides/
   - Display in VisualGuide.jsx component in chat
   - Files: server/core/visualGuideGenerator.js, server/assets/screenshots/, client/src/components/Chat/VisualGuide.jsx
 5. Skill tracker
   - logSkill(userId, skillName, status) — write to skill_events
   - getUserSkills(userId) — list all learned skills
   - getSkillsForReinforcement(userId) — skills not practiced in 7+ days
   - File: server/core/skillTracker.js
 6. Scam detection
   - Keyword patterns: gift cards, wire transfer, IRS, lottery, send money, Bitcoin
   - Warn user with prominent alert in chat
   - Update: server/core/safetyMonitor.js
 7. Context compression
   - After 20 messages in a session, call Claude to summarize older messages
   - Store summary in conversations.context_summary
   - Inject summary into system prompt for continuity
   - Update: server/core/conversationState.js
 8. Tests for v2 features
   - Test step sequencer (advancement, confirmation detection, boundary conditions)
   - Test full conversation flow (multi-turn mock)
   - Files: server/__tests__/stepSequencer.test.js, server/__tests__/conversationFlow.test.js

 ---
 Phase 3 — v3 by April 28 (Polish + Scaffolding Fade + Evaluation)

 Goal: Fade scaffolding, accessibility improvements, skill dashboard, deployment.

 Steps:

 1. Scaffolding fade logic
   - If user completed a skill 3+ times, agent offers: "Want to try this on your own first?"
   - On success: positive reinforcement. On failure: resume guided mode
   - Update: server/core/agentOrchestrator.js, server/core/skillTracker.js
 2. Accessibility improvements
   - Theme toggle: high contrast / large text / default
   - Keyboard navigation throughout
   - Larger step counts (more granular) for users with accessibility needs
   - Update: client/src/styles/globals.css, client/src/components/
 3. Skill history sidebar
   - Sidebar.jsx — shows all learned skills with dates and practice count
   - GET /api/users/:id/skills endpoint
   - Files: client/src/components/Layout/Sidebar.jsx, server/routes/skills.js
 4. Proactive messages (in-app)
   - node-cron job checks for skill reinforcement opportunities
   - Sends in-app notification: "Want to practice [skill] today?"
   - File: server/core/proactiveEngine.js
 5. Deployment
   - Build React → static files served by Express
   - Deploy to Railway or Render
   - Environment variables for secrets
   - Update: server/index.js (serve static), README.md
 6. Evaluation prep
   - Pre/post confidence survey component in React
   - Conversation log export endpoint: GET /api/conversations/:id/export
   - Skill completion rate metrics

 ---
 Key Design Decisions

 WebSocket for real-time chat: Streaming Claude responses token-by-token gives a natural chat feel. Fallback REST endpoint for
 reliability.

 SQLite for v1/v2: Zero setup, single file DB. Same query patterns transfer to PostgreSQL for production. better-sqlite3 is synchronous    
 but fast enough for a class project. If async needed, switch to sqlite3 with promises.

 Elderly-friendly UI defaults: 18px+ base font, high-contrast colors, large buttons, minimal navigation. No complex UI patterns — just a   
 chat window and onboarding wizard.

 Context compression at 20 messages: Bounds token cost while maintaining conversation continuity. Claude summarizes older messages into a  
 compact context string.

 Tool-use agent loop: Claude decides when to use tools (create steps, log skills, flag emergencies) rather than hardcoded routing. More    
 flexible and natural conversation flow.

 ---
 Verification Plan

 Local dev

 1. npm install in root and client/
 2. Set .env with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
 3. npm run dev — starts Express (port 3001) + Vite dev server (port 5173) with proxy
 4. Open http://localhost:5173 in browser

 Automated tests

 - npm test — Jest tests for backend modules
 - Mock Claude API responses with Jest mocks
 - React Testing Library for component tests

 Manual QA checklist per version

 - Onboarding wizard collects name + OS + comfort level
 - Chat message sends and receives response
 - Vocabulary simplification in responses
 - Emergency keyword triggers safety alert
 - (v2) Step-by-step flow with progress bar and confirmation
 - (v2) Annotated screenshot displays in chat
 - (v2) Scam detection warning displays
 - (v3) Skill fade ("try on your own") after 3 completions
 - (v3) Skill history sidebar shows learned skills
 - (v3) Deployed and accessible via public URL

# PC Pal — File-by-File Guide

Every file in the project, what it does, and where it fits.

---

## Root Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `package.json` | Node.js project config. Dependencies, scripts (`npm run dev`, `npm test`) |
| `.env.example` | Template for environment variables. Copy to `.env` and fill in your keys |
| `.env` | Your actual API keys (gitignored — never committed) |
| `.gitignore` | Files git should ignore (node_modules, .env, database files) |
| `jest.config.js` | Test runner config — tells Jest to only look at `server/__tests__/` |
| `README.md` | Project overview and setup instructions |

---

## Server Files

### `server/index.js` — The Entry Point
- Creates the Express HTTP server
- Sets up the WebSocket server on `/ws`
- Mounts REST routes (`/api/users`, `/api/chat`)
- Handles WebSocket message protocol: `init` → `chat` → `response`
- Includes connection cleanup, input validation, and graceful shutdown

### `server/config.js` — Environment Config
- Loads `.env` file via dotenv
- Exports: `{ port, anthropicApiKey, geminiApiKey }`

---

### `server/db/` — Database

| File | What it does |
|------|-------------|
| `schema.sql` | Defines all 7 database tables. Runs automatically on startup. |
| `database.js` | Initializes SQLite via `better-sqlite3`. Enables WAL mode and foreign keys. Exports the `db` instance used by all models. |
| `pcpal.db` | The actual database file (created automatically, gitignored) |

---

### `server/models/` — Data Access Layer

Each model file exports an object with CRUD methods. All use synchronous `better-sqlite3` calls and `uuid` for ID generation.

| File | Table | Key Methods |
|------|-------|------------|
| `User.js` | `users` | `create`, `findById`, `findAll`, `update`, `delete` |
| `Conversation.js` | `conversations` | `create`, `findById`, `findByUserId`, `findActive`, `update`, `close`, `abandonStale` |
| `Message.js` | `messages` | `create`, `findByConversationId`, `getRecent(conversationId, limit=20)` |
| `StepSequence.js` | `step_sequences` | `create`, `findById`, `findByConversationId`, `update` — stores steps as JSON array |
| `SkillEvent.js` | `skill_events` | `create`, `findByUserId`, `findBySkillName` — tracks skill started/completed events |
| `SafetyEvent.js` | `safety_events` | `create`, `findByUserId` — logs emergency and scam detections |
| `UserNote.js` | `user_notes` | `create`, `findByUserId`, `findById`, `delete` — user's saved tips |

---

### `server/core/` — Business Logic (The Brain)

This is where all the important logic lives.

#### `agentOrchestrator.js` — The Main Pipeline (~450 lines)
**This is the most important file in the project.**

- Defines 12 Claude AI tools with their schemas
- `processMessage(text, userId)` — the entry point for every user message
- Pipeline: safety check → mock mode check → user lookup → session management → classification → Claude API call → tool handling loop → vocabulary filtering → save & return
- `handleFunctionCall(name, args, userId, sessionId)` — dispatches tool calls from the AI to the appropriate handler
- `buildSystemPrompt(profileString, user, classification)` — constructs the AI's personality and instructions based on user profile and comfort level
- `buildComfortGuidelines(comfortLevel)` — returns different instruction sets for comfort levels 1, 2-3, and 4-5

#### `mockResponder.js` — Demo Mode (~250 lines)
- Used when no API key is set or `MOCK_MODE=true`
- Pattern-matches user messages (e.g., "copy" → copy/paste guide, "done" → advance step)
- Returns the same response shape as the real orchestrator
- Creates real step sequences, skill events, and notes in the database
- Exercises all UI features without any external API calls

#### `safetyMonitor.js` — Emergency & Scam Detection (~100 lines)
- `checkMessage(text, userId)` — scans every message before the AI sees it
- 10 emergency keyword patterns (word-boundary regex, case-insensitive)
- 8 scam detection patterns (gift cards, wire transfers, IRS, remote access, etc.)
- Logs detections to `SafetyEvent` model
- Returns `{ safe: true/false, type: 'emergency'|'scam'|null, response: string|null }`

#### `taskClassifier.js` — Message Classification (~85 lines)
- `classifyMessage(text, userProfile)` — calls Claude API to classify the message
- Returns: `{ taskType: 'learn_skill'|'troubleshoot'|'follow_up'|'accessibility'|'unknown', topic, urgency }`
- Gracefully falls back to `unknown` on any API error
- Strips markdown code fences from Claude's response before parsing

#### `vocabularyFilter.js` — Jargon Replacement (~100 lines)
- `filterResponse(text, vocabLevel)` — replaces technical terms with plain language
- 3 levels: `basic` (all 20+ substitutions), `intermediate` (8 technical terms only), `standard` (no changes)
- Whole-word matching (won't replace "browsing" when targeting "browser")
- `enforceReadability(text)` — splits sentences >20 words at conjunctions (and, but, or, so, because)

#### `conversationState.js` — Session Management (~70 lines)
- `getOrCreateSession(userId)` — finds the user's active conversation or creates a new one
- `closeSession(sessionId)` — marks a conversation as completed
- `abandonStale()` — marks conversations with no activity for 30+ minutes as abandoned
- `addMessage(sessionId, role, body)` — adds a message to the conversation
- `getSessionMessages(sessionId, limit)` — retrieves recent messages

#### `userProfileManager.js` — Profile Logic (~110 lines)
- `getOrCreateUser(id)` — finds or creates a user record
- `updateProfile(id, fields)` — updates allowed profile fields only
- `getProfileForPrompt(id)` — returns a formatted string for injecting into the AI's system prompt, including name, OS, vocabulary level, comfort level, and skill history with relative timestamps

#### `skillProgression.js` — Learning Chains (~75 lines)
- Defines 3 skill progression chains:
  - `copy_paste → send_email → attach_file`
  - `open_browser → find_wifi → open_settings`
  - `take_screenshot → zoom_text → use_taskbar → restart_computer`
- `getNextSkill(userId)` — walks the chains and finds the first uncompleted skill
- `getSkillStatus(userId)` — returns all skills with completion status

#### `taskClassifier.js` — Message Classification (~85 lines)
- `classifyMessage(text, userProfile)` — calls Claude API to classify the message
- Returns: `{ taskType: 'learn_skill'|'troubleshoot'|'follow_up'|'accessibility'|'unknown', topic, urgency }`
- Gracefully falls back to `unknown` on any API error
- Strips markdown code fences from Claude's response before parsing

#### `vocabularyFilter.js` — Jargon Replacement (~100 lines)
- `filterResponse(text, vocabLevel)` — replaces technical terms with plain language
- 3 levels: `basic` (all 20+ substitutions), `intermediate` (8 technical terms only), `standard` (no changes)
- Whole-word matching (won't replace "browsing" when targeting "browser")
- `enforceReadability(text)` — splits sentences >20 words at conjunctions (and, but, or, so, because)

#### `conversationState.js` — Session Management (~70 lines)
- `getOrCreateSession(userId)` — finds the user's active conversation or creates a new one
- `closeSession(sessionId)` — marks a conversation as completed
- `abandonStale()` — marks conversations with no activity for 30+ minutes as abandoned
- `addMessage(sessionId, role, body)` — adds a message to the conversation
- `getSessionMessages(sessionId, limit)` — retrieves recent messages

#### `userProfileManager.js` — Profile Logic (~110 lines)
- `getOrCreateUser(id)` — finds or creates a user record
- `updateProfile(id, fields)` — updates allowed profile fields only
- `getProfileForPrompt(id)` — returns a formatted string for injecting into the AI's system prompt, including name, OS, vocabulary level, comfort level, and skill history with relative timestamps

#### `skillProgression.js` — Learning Chains (~75 lines)
- Defines 3 skill progression chains:
  - `copy_paste → send_email → attach_file`
  - `open_browser → find_wifi → open_settings`
  - `take_screenshot → zoom_text → use_taskbar → restart_computer`
- `getNextSkill(userId)` — walks the chains and finds the first uncompleted skill
- `getSkillStatus(userId)` — returns all skills with completion status

| File | Endpoints |
|------|----------|
| `users.js` | `POST /api/users` (create), `GET /api/users/:id` (read), `PUT /api/users/:id` (update), `PUT /api/users/:id/onboard` (mark onboarded) |

# Getting Started — For Teammates

Welcome to PC Pal! This guide will get you up and running in 5 minutes.

---

## What is this project?

PC Pal is a web app that helps elderly people learn to use their computer. Users chat with an AI assistant that:
- Explains things in simple language
- Shows visual guide cards with numbered steps and keyboard diagrams
- Tracks what skills they've learned
- Detects emergencies and scams

**You don't need an API key to run it.** The app has a built-in demo mode.

---

## Quick Start

### 1. Clone & Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/COS498-Group-7-Repo.git
cd COS498-Group-7-Repo
npm install
cd client && npm install && cd ..
```

### 2. Create your .env file

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

That's it. The defaults enable demo mode automatically.

### 3. Start the app

```bash
npm run dev
```

This starts two servers:
- **Backend** on http://localhost:3001
- **Frontend** on http://localhost:5173

### 4. Open in your browser

Go to **http://localhost:5173**

You'll see the onboarding wizard. Fill in a name, pick a device, set comfort level, and you're in the chat.

---

## Try These in Demo Mode

| Type this | What happens |
|-----------|-------------|
| "How do I copy and paste?" | Visual guide card appears + step-by-step walkthrough starts |
| "done" or "next" | Advances to the next step |
| "How do I take a screenshot?" | Another visual guide with keyboard shortcuts |
| "What should I learn next?" | Suggests the next skill based on your progress |
| "My notes" | Shows saved tips from your session |
| "Start over" | Clears the conversation |
| "Help" | Lists everything PC Pal can help with |
| "I've fallen" | Triggers the emergency alert system |

---

## Project Structure (High Level)

```
client/           React frontend (what the user sees)
```

119	**Where it falls short:** General-purpose AI assistants are not designed for elderly users and fail them in specific, predictable ways. First, they use technical language without simplification -- ChatGPT will say "navigate to System Preferences" rather than "look for the picture of gears on your screen." Second, they provide too many steps at once: a 7-step instruction set overwhelms a comfort-level-1 user who can process 2 steps at a time. Third, they have no memory across sessions -- the user who learned to send email yesterday is treated as a complete stranger today. Fourth, they have no safety monitoring: if an elderly user mentions they've fallen or describes a scam call, ChatGPT provides generic advice rather than displaying an emergency alert. Perfect! Now I have comprehensive information. Let me compile the thorough summary:

## Comprehensive Summary of PC Pal Project Changes Since Commit b014ee9

### 1. **Electron Desktop App** (electron/main.js and electron/preload.js)

**What it adds:**
- Full Electron desktop application wrapper that embeds the Express server and React frontend
- `electron/main.js`: Starts the Express server on port 3001, creates a BrowserWindow (1100x800 with 480x600 minimum), and loads the React app via http://localhost:3001
- Sets `ELECTRON_MODE=true` environment variable so the server knows it's running as a desktop app
- Implements graceful shutdown: closes server before quitting the app
- Friendly appearance with light blue background (#f0f4f8) optimized for elderly users
- `electron/preload.js`: Exposes minimal, safe APIs via contextBridge (`isDesktopApp` boolean, `platform` property) with full context isolation and nodeIntegration disabled

**Why it matters:** PC Pal now has an installable desktop application entry point alongside the web version, enabling offline/local system diagnostic access without browser sandboxing limitations.

---

### 2. **Agent SDK Orchestrator** (server/core/agentSdkOrchestrator.js)

**How it differs from agentOrchestrator.js:**
- Uses Claude's new `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` (model claude-sonnet-4-20250514) instead of manual tool-use loops
- Replaces the synchronous tool invocation pattern with `query()` async generator that automatically handles tool calls
- MCP server integration: exposes 23 custom PC Pal tools via an in-process MCP server (`createPcPalMcpServer()`)
- System prompt builds "comfort guidelines" based on user.comfort_level (1-3 scale) with different instruction styles (analogies for beginner, numbered steps for intermediate, concise for advanced)
- Automatically injects matched skill prompts into the system context via `skillMatcher.matchSkill()`
- Includes fallback: if Agent SDK fails or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is missing, automatically falls back to original agentOrchestrator
- Integrates quality tracking real-time (records turn number, vocabulary level, OS type, confusion state)
- Supports structured outputs: can extract visual guide IDs from response markers (VISUAL_GUIDE:guideName)

**Key difference:** Agent SDK removes complexity of manual tool invocation and provider detection — Claude handles tool decisions natively with full context of user comfort level and matched skill expertise.

---

### 3. **MCP Server Tools** (server/mcp/pcpalTools.js)

**23 custom MCP tools exposed:**

**System Diagnostics (8 tools):**
1. `get_system_info` — OS, CPU, RAM (used/free %), uptime, disk space
2. `check_network` — Internet connectivity, DNS, Wi-Fi status, IP, latency
3. `list_running_apps` — Running processes with CPU/memory usage
4. `read_error_log` — System/application/crash error logs (system-specific)
5. `run_safe_command` — Allowlisted diagnostic commands only (hostname, ipconfig, ping, etc.)
6. `check_disk_health` — Disk usage, large folders, temp files
7. `check_installed_software` — List apps or search by name
8. `get_battery_status` — Battery level and charging state (laptops)

**Teaching & Skill Tools (7 tools):**
9. `log_skill_started` — Record skill learning begins
10. `suggest_next_skill` — Recommend next skill based on completion history
11. `schedule_skill_review` — Spaced repetition review scheduling
12. `start_step_sequence` — Begin numbered step-by-step walkthrough
13. `advance_step` — Move to next step in sequence
14. `complete_step_sequence` — Mark sequence complete and log skill
15. `show_visual_guide` — Display visual step-by-step card (10 valid guide IDs: copy_paste, take_screenshot, send_email, open_settings, zoom_text, find_wifi, attach_file, open_browser, restart_computer, use_taskbar)

**Safety Tools (2 tools):**
16. `flag_emergency` — Log potential emergency (injury, medical, falling)
17. `analyze_scam_situation` — Structured scam analysis with red flags, risk level, official verification contacts

**User & Notes Tools (4 tools):**
18. `save_note_for_user` — Save helpful tip for later reference
19. `get_user_notes` — Retrieve all user's saved notes
20. `save_user_goal` — Log user's learning goal when they express WHY they want to learn
21. `adjust_vocabulary_level` — Change vocabulary simplification (basic/intermediate/standard)

**Buddy System Tools (2 tools):**
22. `share_progress_with_buddy` — Share skill completion with learning buddy
23. `ask_buddy_for_help` — Send help request to buddy when stuck

Each tool returns `{ content: [{ type: 'text', text: ... }] }` MCP format.

---

### 4. **System Diagnostics** (server/core/systemDiagnostics.js)

**What it runs:**
- **Platform detection:** Identifies Windows, macOS, Linux
- **Command sandbox:** Allowlisted patterns per platform (regex-based), blocks dangerous patterns (rm, sudo, curl, pipes, redirects, package managers)
- **Safe execution:** 10-second timeout, 512KB max output, captures stderr
- **getSystemInfo():** Runs OS-specific commands (ver, wmic on Windows; sw_vers on Mac; /etc/os-release on Linux) to extract version, CPU name, RAM usage %, uptime, hostname, user, disk info
- **checkNetwork():** Pings 8.8.8.8, tests DNS (nslookup google.com), retrieves Wi-Fi status (netsh wlan on Windows, airport on Mac, nmcli on Linux), IP address, and latency to Google
- **listRunningApps():** Platform-specific process listing (tasklist, ps aux, ps aux with sort)
- **readErrorLog():** Accesses Windows Event Viewer (wevtutil), macOS log show with error filtering, Linux journalctl or /var/log/syslog
- **checkDiskHealth():** wmic logicaldisk on Windows, df -h on Mac/Linux, plus folder size breakdown for Desktop/Downloads/Documents, temp files
- **checkInstalledSoftware():** wmic product on Windows, /Applications listing on Mac, dpkg/rpm on Linux with optional search term filtering
- **getBatteryStatus():** wmic path Win32_Battery on Windows, pmset -g batt on Mac, /sys/class/power_supply/BAT0 on Linux
- **runSafeCommand():** Enforces two-layer security — BLOCKED_PATTERNS (command chaining, destructive commands) checked first, then allowlisted commands per platform

**Blocked patterns:** ;, |, `, $, >, rm, del, format, mkfs, dd, sudo, runas, chmod, chown, kill, taskkill, shutdown, reboot, curl, wget, npm, pip, apt, brew, reg, powershell destructive commands

---

### 5. **Chat Feedback System**

**client/src/components/Chat/FeedbackModal.jsx:**
- End-of-chat feedback component (required 1-5 star rating, optional comment up to 2000 chars)
- Accessible design: star buttons as radio group with keyboard navigation, autofocus first star
- Shows "How did I do?" with subtitle "Your feedback helps PC Pal get better"
- Actions: "No thanks" (skip) or "Send feedback" (submit)
- Handles submission state and error display
- Calls `onSubmit({ rating, comment })` on submit, `onSkip()` on dismiss

**server/models/ConversationFeedback.js:**
- SQLite model with validation: rating must be 1-5 integer, conversation_id + user_id required, comment trimmed to 2000 chars
- Enforces UNIQUE constraint on conversation_id (prevents double-submit)
- Methods:
  - `create(data)` — inserts feedback row and returns it
  - `findById(id)` — retrieves single feedback
  - `findByConversationId(conversationId)` — get feedback for a conversation
  - `getAggregateStats()` — returns { count, average_rating, distribution: { 1-5 counts } }

**Flow:** User clicks "End chat" → server closes session → modal shows → user rates + comments → POST to `/api/quality/feedback` → feedback saved to DB → chat resets for new conversation.

---

### 6. **Scam Knowledge Base** (server/assets/scam-knowledge.json)

**What it contains (comprehensive elderly fraud database):**

**Red flags** (16 specific warning signs):
- Creates urgency ("act now or else")
- Requests payment by gift card/wire/crypto
- Asks for remote access
- Says "don't tell anyone"
- Threatens arrest/deportation
- Asks for password/PIN/SSN
- Unsolicited calls
- Caller ID spoofing
- Forces phone call during bank visit
- Email address mismatch
- Spelling/grammar errors
- Too-good-to-be-true offers
- Computer infection claims
- Download/click link requests
- "Move money to safe account"
- Pressure without family consultation

**Never legitimate claims** (9 absolute rules):
- No company ever asks for gift cards
- Social Security can't be "suspended"
- Police don't call to threaten arrest
- Tech companies never demand passwords
- Pop-up unlock demands are fake
- Winning contests you didn't enter is fake
- No legit wire money or crypto requests
- No requests to hide from family
- No requests for prepaid debit card numbers

**12 scam patterns with details:**
1. Tech Support Scam — "computer infected", fake Microsoft alerts, demands remote access
2. IRS/Tax Scam — "back taxes owed", arrest threats
3. Social Security Scam — "number suspended", verification demands
4. Medicare Scam — "need your number", free equipment offers
5. Grandchild Emergency Scam — "I'm in trouble", bail/hospital money
6. Romance Scam — online relationship, money emergencies

Perfect! Now I have comprehensive information. Let me compile the thorough summary:

## Comprehensive Summary of PC Pal Project Changes Since Commit b014ee9

### 1. **Electron Desktop App** (electron/main.js and electron/preload.js)

**What it adds:**
- Full Electron desktop application wrapper that embeds the Express server and React frontend
- `electron/main.js`: Starts the Express server on port 3001, creates a BrowserWindow (1100x800 with 480x600 minimum), and loads the React app via http://localhost:3001
- Sets `ELECTRON_MODE=true` environment variable so the server knows it's running as a desktop app
- Implements graceful shutdown: closes server before quitting the app
- Friendly appearance with light blue background (#f0f4f8) optimized for elderly users
- `electron/preload.js`: Exposes minimal, safe APIs via contextBridge (`isDesktopApp` boolean, `platform` property) with full context isolation and nodeIntegration disabled

**Why it matters:** PC Pal now has an installable desktop application entry point alongside the web version, enabling offline/local system diagnostic access without browser sandboxing limitations.

---

### 2. **Agent SDK Orchestrator** (server/core/agentSdkOrchestrator.js)

**How it differs from agentOrchestrator.js:**
- Uses Claude's new `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` (model claude-sonnet-4-20250514) instead of manual tool-use loops
- Replaces the synchronous tool invocation pattern with `query()` async generator that automatically handles tool calls
- MCP server integration: exposes 23 custom PC Pal tools via an in-process MCP server (`createPcPalMcpServer()`)
- System prompt builds "comfort guidelines" based on user.comfort_level (1-3 scale) with different instruction styles (analogies for beginner, numbered steps for intermediate, concise for advanced)
- Automatically injects matched skill prompts into the system context via `skillMatcher.matchSkill()`
- Includes fallback: if Agent SDK fails or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is missing, automatically falls back to original agentOrchestrator
- Integrates quality tracking real-time (records turn number, vocabulary level, OS type, confusion state)
- Supports structured outputs: can extract visual guide IDs from response markers (VISUAL_GUIDE:guideName)

**Key difference:** Agent SDK removes complexity of manual tool invocation and provider detection — Claude handles tool decisions natively with full context of user comfort level and matched skill expertise.

---

### 3. **MCP Server Tools** (server/mcp/pcpalTools.js)

**23 custom MCP tools exposed:**

**System Diagnostics (8 tools):**
1. `get_system_info` — OS, CPU, RAM (used/free %), uptime, disk space
2. `check_network` — Internet connectivity, DNS, Wi-Fi status, IP, latency
3. `list_running_apps` — Running processes with CPU/memory usage
4. `read_error_log` — System/application/crash error logs (system-specific)
5. `run_safe_command` — Allowlisted diagnostic commands only (hostname, ipconfig, ping, etc.)
6. `check_disk_health` — Disk usage, large folders, temp files
7. `check_installed_software` — List apps or search by name
8. `get_battery_status` — Battery level and charging state (laptops)

**Teaching & Skill Tools (7 tools):**
9. `log_skill_started` — Record skill learning begins
10. `suggest_next_skill` — Recommend next skill based on completion history
11. `schedule_skill_review` — Spaced repetition review scheduling
12. `start_step_sequence` — Begin numbered step-by-step walkthrough
13. `advance_step` — Move to next step in sequence
14. `complete_step_sequence` — Mark sequence complete and log skill
15. `show_visual_guide` — Display visual step-by-step card (10 valid guide IDs: copy_paste, take_screenshot, send_email, open_settings, zoom_text, find_wifi, attach_file, open_browser, restart_computer, use_taskbar)

**Safety Tools (2 tools):**
16. `flag_emergency` — Log potential emergency (injury, medical, falling)
17. `analyze_scam_situation` — Structured scam analysis with red flags, risk level, official verification contacts

**User & Notes Tools (4 tools):**
18. `save_note_for_user` — Save helpful tip for later reference
19. `get_user_notes` — Retrieve all user's saved notes
20. `save_user_goal` — Log user's learning goal when they express WHY they want to learn
21. `adjust_vocabulary_level` — Change vocabulary simplification (basic/intermediate/standard)

**Buddy System Tools (2 tools):**
22. `share_progress_with_buddy` — Share skill completion with learning buddy
23. `ask_buddy_for_help` — Send help request to buddy when stuck

Each tool returns `{ content: [{ type: 'text', text: ... }] }` MCP format.

---

### 4. **System Diagnostics** (server/core/systemDiagnostics.js)

**What it runs:**
- **Platform detection:** Identifies Windows, macOS, Linux
- **Command sandbox:** Allowlisted patterns per platform (regex-based), blocks dangerous patterns (rm, sudo, curl, pipes, redirects, package managers)
- **Safe execution:** 10-second timeout, 512KB max output, captures stderr
- **getSystemInfo():** Runs OS-specific commands (ver, wmic on Windows; sw_vers on Mac; /etc/os-release on Linux) to extract version, CPU name, RAM usage %, uptime, hostname, user, disk info
- **checkNetwork():** Pings 8.8.8.8, tests DNS (nslookup google.com), retrieves Wi-Fi status (netsh wlan on Windows, airport on Mac, nmcli on Linux), IP address, and latency to Google
- **listRunningApps():** Platform-specific process listing (tasklist, ps aux, ps aux with sort)
- **readErrorLog():** Accesses Windows Event Viewer (wevtutil), macOS log show with error filtering, Linux journalctl or /var/log/syslog
- **checkDiskHealth():** wmic logicaldisk on Windows, df -h on Mac/Linux, plus folder size breakdown for Desktop/Downloads/Documents, temp files
- **checkInstalledSoftware():** wmic product on Windows, /Applications listing on Mac, dpkg/rpm on Linux with optional search term filtering
- **getBatteryStatus():** wmic path Win32_Battery on Windows, pmset -g batt on Mac, /sys/class/power_supply/BAT0 on Linux
- **runSafeCommand():** Enforces two-layer security — BLOCKED_PATTERNS (command chaining, destructive commands) checked first, then allowlisted commands per platform

**Blocked patterns:** ;, |, `, $, >, rm, del, format, mkfs, dd, sudo, runas, chmod, chown, kill, taskkill, shutdown, reboot, curl, wget, npm, pip, apt, brew, reg, powershell destructive commands

---

### 5. **Chat Feedback System**

**client/src/components/Chat/FeedbackModal.jsx:**
- End-of-chat feedback component (required 1-5 star rating, optional comment up to 2000 chars)
- Accessible design: star buttons as radio group with keyboard navigation, autofocus first star
- Shows "How did I do?" with subtitle "Your feedback helps PC Pal get better"
- Actions: "No thanks" (skip) or "Send feedback" (submit)
- Handles submission state and error display
- Calls `onSubmit({ rating, comment })` on submit, `onSkip()` on dismiss

**server/models/ConversationFeedback.js:**
- SQLite model with validation: rating must be 1-5 integer, conversation_id + user_id required, comment trimmed to 2000 chars
- Enforces UNIQUE constraint on conversation_id (prevents double-submit)
- Methods:
  - `create(data)` — inserts feedback row and returns it
  - `findById(id)` — retrieves single feedback
  - `findByConversationId(conversationId)` — get feedback for a conversation
  - `getAggregateStats()` — returns { count, average_rating, distribution: { 1-5 counts } }

**Flow:** User clicks "End chat" → server closes session → modal shows → user rates + comments → POST to `/api/quality/feedback` → feedback saved to DB → chat resets for new conversation.

- Category: diagnostics | Difficulty: intermediate
- Prompt: reassure user → call `get_system_info` + `read_error_log` → translate results to plain English → use `start_step_sequence` for fixes → re-run diagnostics after to verify fix

**disk-cleanup.json (id: disk_cleanup)**
- Triggers: "no space", "storage full", "can't save", "hard drive full", "clean up"
- Category: diagnostics | Difficulty: beginner
- Prompt: use `check_disk_health` for ACTUAL usage → translate (e.g., "85% full") → guide cleanup in order (Downloads, Trash, Temp, large files) → NEVER suggest deleting system files → re-run after

**network-fix.json (id: network_fix)**
- Triggers: "no internet", "wifi not working", "pages won't load", "can't get online", "slow internet", "dns"
- Category: diagnostics | Difficulty: intermediate
- Prompt: use `check_network` FIRST before guessing → translate results to plain English → give specific fixes based on actual findings (restart router, forget/rejoin Wi-Fi, flush DNS) → verify with re-run

**scam-check.json (id: scam-check)**
- Triggers: "is this a scam", "is this real", "am I getting scammed", "should I trust", "someone asked me for money"
- Category: security | Difficulty: critical
- Prompt: use `analyze_scam_situation` tool for structured analysis → walk through red flags → NEVER say "it's safe" → always recommend official verification channels → provide real phone numbers

**slow-computer.json (id: slow_computer)**
- Triggers: "computer is slow", "so slow", "laggy", "lagging", "takes forever", "fan is loud", "overheating"
- Category: diagnostics | Difficulty: beginner
- Prompt: call `get_system_info` + `list_running_apps` simultaneously → find causes (RAM 80%+, single app using lots CPU, uptime >3 days, disk >90%) → tell user what found → use `start_step_sequence` (close apps, restart, free space) → celebrate improvement

**system-checkup.json (id: system_checkup)**
- Triggers: "check my computer", "is my computer ok", "health check", "how is my computer", "any problems"
- Category: diagnostics | Difficulty: beginner
- Prompt: run ALL diagnostic tools (system info, network, disk, battery, running apps) → present as friendly "report card" (Memory, Storage, Internet, Battery, Uptime) → use simple ratings ("Looking good!", "Could use attention", "Let's fix this")

---

### 8. **New Test Suites** (90 new tests across 5 files)

**conversationFeedback.test.js** (10 tests)
- Tests ConversationFeedback.create() validation: rating must be 1-5, required fields, comment trimming (2000 char max), blank comment = null
- Tests UNIQUE constraint on conversation_id (prevents double-submit)
- Tests findByConversationId() and getAggregateStats()

**systemDiagnostics.test.js** (29 tests)
- Tests getPlatform() returns valid platform
- Tests getSystemInfo() includes OS, memory, CPU, hostname
- Tests runSafeCommand() sandbox: blocks rm, sudo, curl, wget, pipes, semicolons, package managers, backticks, $(), redirects
- Tests allows hostname, whoami
- Tests checkNetwork(), listRunningApps(), getBatteryStatus(), checkDiskHealth(), checkInstalledSoftware(), readErrorLog()

**mcpServer.test.js** (14 tests)
- Tests diagnostic tools return real system data (getSystemInfo contains "Operating System", checkNetwork contains "Internet Connection", etc.)
- Tests sandbox (blocks rm, sudo, curl, injection) and allows safe commands (hostname, whoami)
- Verifies MCP server module path exists

**mockResponder.test.js** (11 tests)
- Tests gatherDiagnosticContext() returns empty string for non-diagnostic skills
- Tests diagnostic context gathering: slow_computer gathers SYSTEM INFO + RUNNING APPS, network_fix gathers NETWORK STATUS, diagnose_system gathers SYSTEM INFO + RECENT ERRORS, etc.
- Tests system_checkup gathers everything
- Tests includes "NEVER show raw output" instruction

**skillMatcher.test.js** (26 tests)
- Tests skill loading: all 24+ skills have required fields (id, name, triggers, prompt, category, difficulty)
- Tests includes original skills (copy-paste, wifi, send-email, screenshot)
- Tests includes new diagnostic skills (diagnose_system, network_fix, slow_computer, disk_cleanup, app_troubleshoot, battery_power, system_checkup)
- Tests diagnostic routing: "freezing" → diagnose_system, "so slow" → slow_computer, "out of space" → disk_cleanup, "Zoom not working" → app_troubleshoot, "battery dying" → battery_power, "checkup" → system_checkup, "wifi disconnecting" → network_fix
- Tests original skill routing: "how do I copy and paste" → copy-paste, "send email" → send-email, "screenshot" → screenshot
- Tests priority tie-breaking: scam-check prioritized over others
- Tests edge cases: null/empty returns null, case-insensitive, scoring, unrelated input returns null
- Tests buildSkillPrompt() returns skill name and substantial prompt
- Tests diagnostic prompts reference diagnostic tools
- Tests getSkillsSummary() returns multi-line summary of all skills

**Total new tests: 90** (covering Agent SDK, MCP, diagnostics, feedback, skills, safety)

---

### 9. **CLAUDE.md Developer Guide**

**Key guidelines:**
- **Quick start:** Web mode (npm install, npm run dev), Desktop mode (npm run start:desktop), Tests (npm test)
- **Architecture sections:** Agent Layer (agentSdkOrchestrator.js primary, agentOrchestrator.js fallback, pcpalTools.js MCP), Core modules (systemDiagnostics, skillMatcher, safetyMonitor, vocabularyFilter, mockResponder), Skills (24 JSON definitions), Models (14 SQLite tables), Frontend (React 19 + Vite), Desktop (Electron)
- **Adding MCP tool:** Define with `tool()` from Agent SDK, add to tools array
- **Adding skill:** Create JSON in server/skills/ with id, name, description, triggers, category, difficulty, prompt
- **Provider flexibility:** Claude direct, Claude via Bedrock, Claude via Vertex, LiteLLM proxy support, MCP tools fully provider-agnostic
- **Safety rules:** systemDiagnostics allowlist, dangerous patterns always blocked, safety monitor runs before AI, translate raw output to plain English
- **Testing:** 169 total tests across 8 suites, specific test commands per module
- **Deployment:** Docker/HF Spaces for web (port 7860), Electron for desktop, mock mode works without API key

---

### 10. **Schema Changes** (server/db/schema.sql)

**New tables added (2):**

1. **conversation_feedback** (end-of-chat ratings)
   - id (UUID primary key)
   - conversation_id (TEXT UNIQUE — prevents double-submit)
   - user_id (TEXT)
   - rating (INTEGER CHECK 1-5)
   - comment (TEXT)
   - created_at (timestamp)
   - Foreign keys to conversations and users

2. **scam_check_events** (scam analysis logging)
   - id (UUID primary key)
   - user_id (TEXT)
   - conversation_id (TEXT)
   - situation_summary (TEXT)
   - claimed_organization (TEXT optional)
   - red_flags (TEXT — JSON array stored as string)
   - risk_level (TEXT — high/medium/low)
   - recommended_action (TEXT)
   - verification_contact (TEXT optional)
   - created_at (timestamp)
   - Foreign keys to users and conversations

**Existing tables preserved:** All 12 original tables (users, conversations, messages, step_sequences, skill_events, safety_events, user_notes, buddy_pairs, progress_shares, help_requests, skill_reviews, user_goals, conversation_quality_events, conversation_quality_summaries) remain unchanged.

---

### 11. **Changes to Existing Core Files**

**server/core/agentOrchestrator.js:**
- Added imports: ScamCheckEvent, scamKnowledge, systemDiagnostics, skillMatcher
- Added `analyze_scam_situation` tool (structured scam analysis with red flags, risk level, verification contacts)
- Added 8 desktop diagnostic tools as fallback: get_system_info, check_network, list_running_apps, read_error_log, run_safe_command, check_disk_health, check_installed_software, get_battery_status
- These tools have full input schemas and descriptions so they work in the fallback orchestrator too

**server/core/safetyMonitor.js:**
- Added `SCAM_QUESTION_PATTERNS` (16 regex patterns for detecting when user ASKS about scam vs. describing active scam)
- Changed behavior: scam questions now pass through to Claude as type: 'scam_question' (with event logged) rather than blocking
- Clarified emergency check runs first (highest priority), scam questions get pass-through, active scam descriptions get blocked with warning

**server/core/mockResponder.js:**
- Added `gatherDiagnosticContext(skill)` function that returns real system data based on skill type
- For each diagnostic skill (slow_computer, network_fix, diagnose_system, disk_cleanup, app_troubleshoot, battery_power, system_checkup), collects relevant system info
- Injects collected data into prompt with instruction: "translate to plain language — NEVER show raw output"
- Exports gatherDiagnosticContext for testing

**server/index.js:**
- Changed default orchestrator selection: tries agentSdkOrchestrator first with try/catch fallback to agentOrchestrator
- WebSocket init handler now retrieves session and returns conversationId in `init_ack` message
- Added new `end_chat` message type: closes active session and triggers feedback modal
- Added `conversationId` and `endedConversationId` fields to chat response message

**server/routes/quality.js:**
- POST `/api/quality/feedback` — saves 1-5 star rating + optional comment, validates conversation ownership, enforces UNIQUE constraint, closes session after feedback
- POST `/api/quality/feedback/skip` — user dismissed feedback modal; still closes session for clean lifecycle
- GET `/stats` now includes feedback aggregate stats (count, average_rating, distribution)

---

### 12. **Changes to Frontend**

**client/src/hooks/useChat.js:**
- Added conversationId state tracking (from init_ack message)
- Added feedbackPrompt state and modal control flow
- Added `endChat()` callback that sends `end_chat` message to server
- Added `submitFeedback({ rating, comment })` that POSTs to `/api/quality/feedback` and resets chat
- Added `skipFeedback()` that POSTs to `/api/quality/feedback/skip` and resets chat
- Added `resetChatLocally()` callback to clear messages, sequence, conversation state
- Returns expanded object with feedback workflow callbacks

**client/src/components/Chat/ChatWindow.jsx:**
- Added FeedbackModal import
- Added "End chat" button at top of chat (disabled until user has sent at least one message)
- Button shows feedback modal when clicked
- Modal calls submitFeedback or skipFeedback based on user action
- Added conditional rendering: `{feedbackPrompt && <FeedbackModal ... />}`
- New chat-header div with end button styling

**client/src/components/Chat/ChatWindow.css:**
- New `.chat-header` and `.chat-header__end-btn` styles (positioning, button state styling)

**FeedbackModal.jsx** (brand new component):
- 1-5 star rating interface with hover preview
- Optional comment textarea (max 2000 chars with visual counter)
- "No thanks" and "Send feedback" buttons
- Accessible (aria labels, radio group semantics, keyboard navigation)
- Loading state and error display

**FeedbackModal.css** (brand new):
- Overlay with modal styling (white card, shadow, centered)
- Star rating styles (filled/unfilled stars, hover effects)
- Textarea and button styling

---

### 13. **package.json Changes**

**New dependencies:**
- `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` (v0.2.108) — Agent SDK with MCP server support
- `zod` (v4.3.6) — Schema validation for tool parameters

**New devDependencies:**
- `electron` (v41.2.0) — Desktop app framework
- `@electron/rebuild` (v4.0.3) — Rebuilds native modules for Electron

**Updated scripts:**
- Added `electron`, `electron:dev`, `build:client`, `electron:rebuild`, `start:desktop`
- `start:desktop` chain: rebuild native modules → build React → launch Electron

**Version bump:** 1.0.0 → 1.1.0
**Description update:** Now mentions "desktop edition with system diagnostics"
**Main entry point change:** package.json main field changed from server/index.js to electron/main.js (for npm start to launch Electron)

---

### Summary Statistics

**New Files Added: 18**
- Electron: 2 (main.js, preload.js)
- MCP Server: 1 (pcpalTools.js)
- System Diagnostics: 1 (systemDiagnostics.js)
- New Skills: 8 JSON files (app-troubleshoot, battery-power, diagnose-system, disk-cleanup, network-fix, scam-check, slow-computer, system-checkup)
- Models: 2 (ConversationFeedback.js, ScamCheckEvent.js)
- Frontend: 3 (FeedbackModal.jsx, FeedbackModal.css, + .test.js updates)
- Orchestrator: 1 (agentSdkOrchestrator.js)
- Tests: 5 new test suites with 90 tests total

**Files Modified: 23**
- Database: 1 (schema.sql)
- Server: 6 (index.js, 3 core modules, 2 routes/models)
- Frontend: 3 (useChat.js, ChatWindow.jsx + CSS)
- Config: 3 (.env.example, package.json, CLAUDE.md)

**Key Architectural Shifts:**
1. Added desktop (Electron) as first-class deployment option alongside web
2. Replaced manual tool orchestration with Claude Agent SDK + MCP for provider flexibility
3. Integrated real system diagnostics into fallback mode (mockResponder now gathers actual system data)
4. Enhanced safety: separated scam questions (pass-through to Claude) from active scam alerts (still blocked)
5. Added user feedback loop: end-of-chat ratings + comments to drive continuous improvement
6. 8 new diagnostic skills targeting elderly user pain points (slow computer, full disk, network, battery, apps crashing, etc.)

**Testing:** 90 new tests covering Agent SDK, MCP, system diagnostics, feedback model, skill routing, and security sandbox enforcement.

Here's what's new since our last session:

---

## New in PC Pal v1.1.0 — 4 Major Features

### 1. Electron Desktop App
New [electron/](electron/) folder with [main.js](electron/main.js) and [preload.js](electron/preload.js). PC Pal can now run as an installable desktop app (1100x800 window, elderly-friendly light blue background). Launches with `npm run start:desktop`. This unlocks real system access for diagnostics — something browser sandboxing prevents.

### 2. Agent SDK + MCP Integration
- **[agentSdkOrchestrator.js](server/core/agentSdkOrchestrator.js)** — New primary orchestrator using `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` instead of manual tool-use loops. Falls back to the original orchestrator if it fails.
- **[pcpalTools.js](server/mcp/pcpalTools.js)** — MCP server exposing **23 tools** (8 system diagnostics, 7 teaching/skill, 2 safety, 4 user/notes, 2 buddy). This makes tools provider-agnostic (works with Claude direct, Bedrock, Vertex, LiteLLM).

### 3. System Diagnostics
**[systemDiagnostics.js](server/core/systemDiagnostics.js)** — 447 lines of cross-platform (Windows/macOS/Linux) diagnostic capabilities:
- System info (OS, CPU, RAM, disk)
- Network checks (connectivity, DNS, Wi-Fi, latency)
- Running apps with resource usage
- Error log reading
- Disk health and cleanup recommendations
- Battery status
- Sandboxed command execution (strict allowlist, blocks all destructive commands)

**8 new skill definitions** in [server/skills/](server/skills/) to trigger diagnostics: `slow-computer`, `network-fix`, `diagnose-system`, `disk-cleanup`, `app-troubleshoot`, `battery-power`, `system-checkup`, `scam-check`

### 4. Chat Feedback System
- **[FeedbackModal.jsx](client/src/components/Chat/FeedbackModal.jsx)** — End-of-chat 1-5 star rating + optional comment
- **[ConversationFeedback.js](server/models/ConversationFeedback.js)** — New model with aggregate stats
- Flow: "End chat" button in [ChatWindow.jsx](client/src/components/Chat/ChatWindow.jsx) → modal → rating saved via `/api/quality/feedback`

---

## Other Notable Changes

| Area | What Changed |
|------|-------------|
| **Safety** | [safetyMonitor.js](server/core/safetyMonitor.js) now distinguishes scam *questions* (pass to Claude for analysis) from active scam *alerts* (still blocked). New [scam-knowledge.json](server/assets/scam-knowledge.json) with 12 scam patterns, 16 red flags, 13 verification contacts |
| **Schema** | 2 new tables: `conversation_feedback` and `scam_check_events` (now **16 total**) |
| **Models** | 2 new: [ConversationFeedback.js](server/models/ConversationFeedback.js), [ScamCheckEvent.js](server/models/ScamCheckEvent.js) |
| **Mock mode** | [mockResponder.js](server/core/mockResponder.js) now gathers *real* system data for diagnostic skills |
| **Tests** | **90 new tests** across 5 new suites (total now ~159). Covers diagnostics sandbox, MCP tools, feedback validation, skill routing, mock responder |
| **Config** | [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) added with developer guidelines. Version bumped to 1.1.0. New deps: `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`, `zod`, `electron` |
| **Skills** | Now **24 skill definitions** (was 16), up from 10 visual guides |

1	# PC Pal — Architecture Overview
2	
3	## What is PC Pal?
4	
5	PC Pal is a web-based AI chat assistant that helps elderly and beginner computer users learn basic PC skills. Think of it as a patient, friendly grandchild who teaches grandparents how to use their computer — through a simple chat interface with visual guides.
6	
7	A user opens the app in their browser, goes through a quick onboarding (name, device, comfort level), and then chats with the AI. The AI responds with simple language, visual step-by-step guide cards, keyboard diagrams, and progress tracking.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## How It All Fits Together
12	
13	```
14	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
15	│            USER'S BROWSER  or  ELECTRON APP          │
16	│                                                     │
17	│  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌───────────┐ │
18	│  │  Onboarding  │  │  Chat Window │  │  Visual   │ │
19	│  │  Wizard      │  │  + Messages  │  │  Guides   │ │
20	│  └──────────────┘  └──────┬───────┘  └───────────┘ │
21	│                           │                         │
22	│                    WebSocket / REST                  │

25	                            ▼

27	│                   EXPRESS SERVER                     │
28	│                   (Node.js, port 3001)               │
29	│                                                     │
30	│  1. Safety Monitor    ──→  Check for emergencies    │
31	│  2. Task Classifier   ──→  What kind of question?   │

51	## The Message Pipeline
52	
53	Every time a user sends a message, it flows through this pipeline:
...
54	### Step 2: User Lookup
55	**File:** `server/core/userProfileManager.js`
56	
57	The user's profile is loaded from the database — their name, OS type, comfort level (1-5), vocabulary level, and skill history. This information is injected into the AI's system prompt so it can personalize its responses.
58	
59	### Step 3: Mock Mode Check
60	**File:** `server/core/mockResponder.js`
61	
62	If no API key is set (or `MOCK_MODE=true`), the pipeline skips the AI and uses pre-written pattern-matched responses instead. The mock responder still creates step sequences, logs skills, and saves notes — it exercises all the same features as the real AI. For diagnostic skills, the mock responder injects real system diagnostic data (battery, disk, network) into Claude CLI prompts.
63	
64	### Step 4: Task Classification
65	**File:** `server/core/taskClassifier.js`
66	
67	The message is classified into a type: `learn_skill`, `troubleshoot`, `follow_up`, `accessibility`, or `unknown`. This classification is passed to the AI along with the urgency level (low/medium/high), so it knows how to prioritize its response.
68	
69	### Step 4b: Skill Matching
70	**File:** `server/core/skillMatcher.js`
71	
72	The user's message is matched against the 24 skill definitions in `server/skills/`. If a match is found, the skill's specialized prompt is injected into the system prompt so Claude has task-specific expertise. Matching uses keyword triggers with difficulty-based priority tie-breaking (critical skills outrank beginner skills when multiple match).
73	
74	### Step 5: AI Agent (Claude)
75	**File:** `server/core/agentSdkOrchestrator.js` (primary) / `server/core/agentOrchestrator.js` (fallback)
76	
77	This is the core of the app. The primary path uses the **Agent SDK orchestrator**, which calls the Agent SDK's `query()` function with MCP tools. If the Agent SDK is unavailable, the server falls back to the **manual orchestrator** with its while-loop tool handling.
78	
79	The AI receives:
80	- The user's message
81	- The conversation history (last 20 messages)
82	- The user's profile (name, OS, comfort level, skills)
83	- The task classification
84	- Matched skill prompts (if any)
85	- A system prompt with 25 tools it can call (via MCP)
86	
87	The AI generates a response and may call tools like `show_visual_guide`, `start_step_sequence`, or any of the 8 system diagnostic tools. Tool calls are processed in a loop (up to 10 rounds) — the AI can call multiple tools before giving its final text answer.
88	
89	### Step 6: Vocabulary Filter
90	**File:** `server/core/vocabularyFilter.js`
91	
92	The AI's response is filtered to replace technical jargon with simple language. "Browser" becomes "internet app", "URL" becomes "web address", "attachment" becomes "file in the email", etc. Sentences longer than 20 words are split at natural break points.
93	
94	### Step 7: Save & Respond
95	
96	The response is saved to the database and sent back to the user via WebSocket (or REST). The response includes:
97	- `text` — the message text
98	- `guideId` — which visual guide to show (if any)
99	- `stepSequence` — step progress data (if any)
100	- `safetyAlert` — emergency/scam alert (if any)
101	
102	---
103	
104	## The 25 AI Tools
105	
106	When the Claude AI is processing a message, it can decide to call any of these tools. All 25 are exposed as provider-agnostic MCP tools via `server/mcp/pcpalTools.js`.
107	
108	### Core Teaching & Interaction Tools (17)
109	
110	| Tool | What it does | When the AI uses it |
