The source images must already exist as PNG/JPG files in `software-images/`. --- ### 2. **skillImages.js** — IMAGE REGISTRY MAPPING **File:** `/c/Users/DELL/Documents/GitHub/COS498-Group-7-Repo/server/core/skillImages.js` (Lines 1-41) **Data Structure:** ```javascript const SKILL_IMAGES = { // Empty object — designed to be populated // Intended shape: // skillId: { // osType: [ // { file: 'filename.png', alt: 'Description' }, // ... // ] // } } ``` **API:** - `getImagesForSkill(skillId, osType)` → Returns array of `{url: '/images/filename.png', alt: 'caption'}` or null - `hasImages(skillId, osType)` → Boolean check - Returns URLs as `/images/{filename}` (relative path, served from Express route) **Current Status:** **EMPTY** — Designed but NOT yet populated. No skill→image mappings exist currently. This is where your reference library would connect. --- ### 3. **pcpalTools.js** — MCP TOOL DEFINITIONS **File:** `/c/Users/DELL/Documents/GitHub/COS498-Group-7-Repo/server/mcp/pcpalTools.js` (Lines 1-580) **Key Tool: `create_guide`** (Lines 509-531) ```javascript const createGuide = tool( 'create_guide', 'Create an interactive guide artifact...', { title: z.string(), // Guide title description: z.string().optional(), // One-sentence summary steps: z.array(z.object({ text: z.string(), // Plain English description command: z.string().optional(), // Terminal command (copy/run UI) note: z.string().optional(), // Tip or warning })) }, async (args) => { const guide = { title: args.title, description: args.description || null, steps: args.steps, }; _lastGuide = guide; // Store in module-level variable return textResult(`Guide "${args.title}" created...`); } ); ``` **CRITICAL:** Each step object has `{text, command?, note?}` — **NO image field per step yet**. This is where you'd add step-level images if needed. **Related Tools:** - `show_visual_guide` (Lines 421-431) — References VALID_GUIDE_IDs from guideRegistry (copy_paste, take_screenshot, etc.) - `find_youtube_videos` (Lines 435-449) — Returns structured video data with `YOUTUBE_VIDEOS:` JSON marker - `createFindings` (Lines 488-505) — Diagnostic findings artifact with `{title, findings: [{label, value, status}]}` **Artifact Flow:** - Tools store artifacts in module-level variables (`_lastGuide`, `_lastFindings`) - `getAndClearLastGuide()` / `getAndClearLastFindings()` — called by orchestrator after MCP query completes - Orchestrator returns these in response object: `{guide, findings}` --- ### 4. **server/index.js** — STATIC IMAGE SERVING **File:** `/c/Users/DELL/Documents/GitHub/COS498-Group-7-Repo/server/index.js` (Line 33) **Express Route:** ```javascript app.use('/images', express.static(path.join(__dirname, 'assets', 'annotated'))); ``` **What This Does:** - Serves files from `server/assets/annotated/` directory via `/images/` URL path - Example: `server/assets/annotated/iphone-settings-tap-wifi.png` → accessible at `http://localhost:3001/images/iphone-settings-tap-wifi.png` - Static serving means files must exist on disk (not generated on-demand) **WebSocket Message Format** (Lines 472-482): ```javascript ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'response', text: result.response, safetyAlert: result.safetyAlert, stepSequence: result.stepSequence || null, videos: result.videos || null, guide: result.guide || null, // ← Artifact from _lastGuide findings: result.findings || null, // ← Artifact from _lastFindings endedConversationId: result.endedConversationId || null, conversationId: result.conversationId || null, })); ``` --- ### 5. **guideRegistry.js** — VISUAL GUIDE DATA **File:** `/c/Users/DELL/Documents/GitHub/COS498-Group-7-Repo/client/src/components/Chat/guideRegistry.js` (Lines 1-326) **Data Structure:** ```javascript export const guideRegistry = { copy_paste: { title: 'How to Copy and Paste', variants: { Windows: [ { num: 1, text: '...', keys: null }, { num: 2, text: '...', keys: ['Ctrl', 'C'] }, ... ], Mac: [...], iPhone: [...], Android: [...] } }, take_screenshot: { ... }, // ... 10 guides total } ``` **Per-Step Structure:** - `num` — step number (1, 2, 3, ...) - `text` — very simple, no jargon (e.g., "Click at the very start of the words...") - `keys` — optional array of keyboard shortcuts to display as badge (e.g., ['Ctrl', 'C']) - **NOTE: No image field per step** **OS Variants:** Supports Windows, Mac, iPhone, Android. Device detection in VisualGuide.jsx (line 22). **Current Guides (10 total):** copy_paste, take_screenshot, send_email, open_settings, zoom_text, find_wifi, attach_file, open_browser, restart_computer, use_taskbar --- ### 6. **VisualGuide.jsx** — VISUAL GUIDE RENDERER **File:** `/c/Users/DELL/Documents/GitHub/COS498-Group-7-Repo/client/src/components/Chat/VisualGuide.jsx` (Lines 1-67) **Props:** - `taskId` — Key in guideRegistry (e.g., "copy_paste") - `osType` — Device type (defaults to "Windows") **Rendering:** ```jsx
    {steps.map((step) => (
  1. {step.num}

    {step.text}

    {step.keys && (
    {step.keys.map((key) => {key})}
    )}
    2. ))}
``` **Current Capabilities:** - Numbered steps with text - Optional keyboard shortcut badges - **NO image support per step** - Called explicitly via `show_visual_guide` tool (hardcoded guide IDs) --- ### 7. **CommandGuide.jsx** — TERMINAL COMMAND ARTIFACT RENDERER **File:** `/c/Users/DELL/Documents/GitHub/COS498-Group-7-Repo/client/src/components/Chat/CommandGuide.jsx` (Lines 1-116) **Props:** ```javascript { guide: { title: string, description?: string, steps: [{ text: string, command?: string, note?: string }] }, onRunCommand?: (command: string) => void, commandResults?: Record, embedded?: boolean } ``` **Rendering:** - Collapsible header with title (unless `embedded=true` for SidePanel) - Ordered list of steps - Each step shows: - `text` — description - Optional code block with command - Copy + Run buttons (Run only if onRunCommand provided) - Command output display (pre tag with error styling) - Optional note (warning/tip) **Per-Step Structure:** `{text, command?, note?}` — **still no image field** **Key Pattern:** Command results are tracked by command string as key: ```javascript commandResults[step.command] = { output, running, error } ``` --- ### 8. **SidePanel.jsx** — MULTI-ARTIFACT VIEWER **File:** `/c/Users/DELL/Documents/GitHub/COS498-Group-7-Repo/client/src/components/Chat/SidePanel.jsx` (Lines 1-97) **Purpose:** Right-side panel showing one artifact at a time with navigation **Artifact Types Supported:** 1. `findings` — DiagnosticFindings (from createFindings tool) 2. `guide` — CommandGuide (from createGuide tool) 3. `videos` — YouTubeEmbed (from findYoutubeVideos) 4. `resources` — ResourcesContent (from gather_resources message type) **Rendering Order:** ```jsx {artifact.findings && } {artifact.guide && } {artifact.videos && } {artifact.resources && } ``` **Multi-Artifact Support:** - Navigation arrows to switch between artifacts (`activeIndex` in artifacts array) - "Inline" button to move artifact into chat body - "Close" button to dismiss - Label shows `title` or `topic` depending on type **Key Detail:** One artifact per message. If a message has both findings AND guide, they appear together in one artifact card (lines 24-30 ChatWindow.jsx). --- ### 9. **EXISTING IMAGE ASSETS** **Directory:** `/c/Users/DELL/Documents/GitHub/COS498-Group-7-Repo/server/assets/` **Current Structure:** ``` assets/ ├── annotated/ (4 iPhone screenshots) │ ├── iphone-settings-overview.png │ ├── iphone-settings-tap-wifi.png │ ├── iphone-wifi-toggle.png │ └── iphone-wifi-select-network.png ├── generated/ (24 procedural images) │ ├── attach_file_keyboard.png │ ├── attach_file_screen.png │ ├── copy_paste_keyboard.png │ ├── copy_paste_screen.png │ ├── find_wifi_keyboard.png │ ├── find_wifi_screen.png │ ├── open_browser_keyboard.png │ ├── open_browser_screen.png │ ├── open_settings_keyboard.png │ ├── open_settings_screen.png │ ├── restart_computer_keyboard.png │ ├── restart_computer_screen.png │ ├── send_email_keyboard.png │ ├── send_email_screen.png │ ├── take_screenshot_keyboard.png │ ├── take_screenshot_screen.png │ ├── use_taskbar_keyboard.png │ ├── use_taskbar_screen.png │ ├── zoom_text_keyboard.png │ └── zoom_text_screen.png ├── software-images/ (Source images for annotator) │ ├── IOS-Settings.png │ ├── IOS-Settings-WiFi.png │ └── IOS-Settings-Icon.jpg ├── vocabulary/ │ └── basicSubstitutions.json └── scam-knowledge.json ``` **`/images` Route Serves:** Only files from `annotated/` directory currently --- ### 10. **ARTIFACT FLOW: MCP TOOL → SERVER → CLIENT** **Complete Journey:** 1. **Client sends message** → WebSocket: `{type: 'chat', text: 'how to copy?', userId}` 2. **Server: agentSdkOrchestrator.processMessage()** (agentSdkOrchestrator.js:155-315) - Sets `setActiveUserContext(userId, sessionId)` (line 201) - Calls `query()` with MCP server - Claude calls `create_guide` tool with steps 3. **MCP Tool: create_guide** (pcpalTools.js:509-531) - Builds `guide = {title, description, steps}` - Stores in module var: `_lastGuide = guide` - Returns text response: "Guide created..." 4. **Orchestrator Extraction** (agentSdkOrchestrator.js:264-265) ```javascript const guide = getAndClearLastGuide(); // Retrieves _lastGuide const findings = getAndClearLastFindings(); ``` 5. **Server Response Object** (agentSdkOrchestrator.js:299-310) ```javascript return { response: filteredResponse, guide: guide || null, // ← Passed to client findings: findings || null, videos: videos && videos.length > 0 ? videos : null, ... } ``` 6. **WebSocket Send** (index.js:472-482) ```javascript ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'response', guide: result.guide, // ← JSON stringified ... })) ``` 7. **Client: useChat.js Receives** (useChat.js:88-118) - Parses WebSocket message - Adds to messages array: ```javascript { id: nextId(), role: 'assistant', text: data.text, guide: data.guide || null, // ← Stored here ... } ``` 8. **Chat Rendering: MessageBubble.jsx** (MessageBubble.jsx:54-123) - If `inlineMode=true`: renders `` - Else: shows tag button "Click to view" 9. **Side Panel: SidePanel.jsx** (SidePanel.jsx:65-96) - Displays full guide in right panel when not inline - User can toggle between inline/side modes --- ### 11. **GUIDE STEP STRUCTURE — CURRENT vs. NEEDED** **Current Step Object:** ```javascript { text: string, // What to do command?: string, // Optional: terminal command note?: string, // Optional: tip/warning } ``` **For Reference Image Library, You'd Need:** ```javascript { text: string, command?: string, note?: string, image?: { // ← NEW url: string, // e.g., '/images/yahoo-compose-button.png' alt: string, // alt text position?: 'left'|'right'|'above'|'below' // optional layout hint } } ``` **OR multiple images per step:** ```javascript { text: string, images?: [{ url, alt }, ...], // ← Array of reference images command?: string, note?: string, } ``` --- ### 12. **KEY ARCHITECTURAL INSIGHTS** **Single Source of Truth for Guide IDs:** - `VALID_GUIDE_IDS` in sharedConstants.js (lines 13-17) - Defines the 10 pre-built guides in guideRegistry.js - Used by both orchestrators and pcpalTools.js **Artifact Pattern (Reusable):** - Module-level variables store artifacts during MCP query - `getAndClear` functions prevent duplicates - Returned in response object to client - No type field needed — client infers type from which property is set (guide, findings, resources, videos) **Image Serving:** - Static only (no dynamic generation) - Express route `/images` → `server/assets/annotated/` - Relative URLs in responses: `{url: '/images/filename.png'}` **Step-by-Step Teaching Pattern:** - `startStepSequence` — for interactive walkthroughs with "next" buttons - `create_guide` — for static instruction lists with optional commands - Two different tools for two different UX patterns **No Per-Step Image Support Yet:** - `create_guide` steps are `{text, command?, note?}` only - Reference image library would require schema change --- ### SUMMARY FOR REFERENCE IMAGE LIBRARY DESIGN To add reference image support, you'd need to: 1. **Populate `skillImages.js`** with mappings: ```javascript SKILL_IMAGES = { 'copy_paste': { 'Windows': [ { file: 'yahoo-compose-button.png', alt: 'Yellow Compose button in Yahoo Mail' }, { file: 'chrome-icon.png', alt: 'Chrome browser icon on taskbar' } ] } } ``` 2. **Add images to `server/assets/annotated/`** (or new subdirectory) 3. **Extend `create_guide` step schema:** ```javascript steps: z.array(z.object({ text: z.string(), command?: z.string(), note?: z.string(), image?: z.object({ // ← NEW url: z.string(), alt: z.string(), }).optional() })) ``` 4. **Update `CommandGuide.jsx`** to render images: ```jsx {step.image && } ``` 5. **Update client message structure** to pass images through WebSocket 6. **Use `getImagesForSkill()`** helper to auto-attach images when a skill is matched All the infrastructure is already there — you just need to populate the registry and extend the schema!

I'm designing a reference image library for PC Pal, an AI tutor for elderly users. When the agent guides a user through a task (e.g., "send an email"), each guide step should optionally display a reference image showing what the button/icon looks like (e.g., "Yahoo Compose button").

## Existing Infrastructure (already in place)

**Server-side:**
- `server/core/imageAnnotator.js` — Can draw circles/arrows/labels on source images using @napi-rs/canvas. Already generates 4 iPhone annotated screenshots on startup.
- `server/core/skillImages.js` — Registry mapping skill IDs to images. Has API: `getImagesForSkill(skillId, osType)` returns `[{url, alt}]`. **Currently empty (not populated).**
- `server/index.js` line 33: `app.use('/images', express.static(path.join(__dirname, 'assets', 'annotated')));` — Serves images from `server/assets/annotated/` at URL `/images/*`
- `server/mcp/pcpalTools.js` — MCP tool `create_guide` with schema: `{title, description?, steps: [{text, command?, note?}]}`. **No image field per step yet.** Each tool stores artifact in module-level var, retrieved via `getAndClearLastGuide()`.
- Artifact flow: MCP tool → module variable → orchestrator extracts → server sends via WebSocket → client renders.

**Client-side:**
- `client/src/components/Chat/CommandGuide.jsx` — Renders guide artifacts. Each step currently shows: text + optional command (with copy/run buttons) + optional note. **No image rendering yet.**
- `client/src/components/Chat/VisualGuide.jsx` — Separate component for pre-built `show_visual_guide` tool (reads from `guideRegistry.js`). Also no image support.
- `client/src/components/Chat/SidePanel.jsx` — Multi-artifact side panel. Currently supports: findings, guide, videos, resources.
- `client/src/components/Chat/guideRegistry.js` — 10 pre-built guides (copy_paste, take_screenshot, etc.) with OS variants. No images per step.

**Existing assets:**
```
server/assets/
├── annotated/ (4 iPhone screenshots)
├── generated/ (20 procedurally generated images, unused?)
├── software-images/ (source images for annotator)
└── vocabulary/, scam-knowledge.json
```

## Requirements for the Image Library

1. **Library must be GENERIC across all 28 skills** (email, video call, messaging, wifi, etc.) — not email-specific
2. Agent should be able to reference images by a clear ID like `yahoo-compose-button` or `windows-taskbar`
3. Agent should know which images are available without me having to list all in the prompt
4. Images should appear in guide steps shown in the side panel (CommandGuide.jsx)
5. Graceful fallback if agent references an image that doesn't exist
6. Easy to ADD new images later (drop file in folder, add entry to registry)
7. Images should be categorized by task area (email, browser, system-windows, system-mac, etc.)

## Design Questions to Answer

### A. How does the agent reference images?

**Option 1: Extend `create_guide` schema to include optional image per step**
```javascript
steps: [{
  text: "Click the Compose button",
  image: { id: "yahoo-compose-button" },
  command?, note?
}]
```
Pros: One tool call, everything in one place
Cons: Larger schema, agent has to remember IDs

**Option 2: New separate tool `show_ui_reference(image_id)` that attaches to the last guide**
Pros: Simpler schema for create_guide
Cons: Two tool calls required for every image

**Option 3: Extend `create_guide` AND accept image URLs directly (agent picks from known list)**
Pros: Flexible
Cons: Agent might hallucinate URLs

**I prefer Option 1.** Confirm or suggest better.

### B. How does the agent KNOW which image IDs exist?

Options:
1. **Inject the full list into the system prompt** — accurate, but bloats prompt if library grows
2. **Agent calls `list_ui_references()` tool when needed** — scales better but adds latency
3. **Auto-match based on skill** — `skillImages.js` returns relevant images for the matched skill, injected into system prompt only when that skill matches
4. **Hybrid: system prompt has category-level hints + detailed tool for lookup**

**I prefer Option 3** — when the skill matches `send-email`, only email-related image IDs get injected. Scales naturally.

### C. Where do images live on disk?

Current `/images` URL serves `server/assets/annotated/`. Options:
1. Reuse `annotated/` and put everything there (flat)
2. Organize by category: `server/assets/ui-references/email/`, `/browser/`, etc., and update Express route
3. Keep a JSON registry that maps image IDs to file paths (decoupling ID from disk layout)

**I prefer Option 3** for long-term flexibility. A JSON registry means we can reorganize files without breaking IDs.

### D. Schema for the image in a guide step

Simple option:
```javascript
step.image = { id: "yahoo-compose-button" }
```

Server expands this to:
```javascript
step.image = {
  id: "yahoo-compose-button",
  url: "/images/yahoo-compose-button.png",
  alt: "Yellow Compose button in Yahoo Mail, upper left corner"
}
```

Client renders the URL.

### E. What about image annotation (arrows, circles)?

The `imageAnnotator.js` already exists. Do we:
1. **Phase 1 (now):** Static images only. Ship without annotation.
2. **Phase 2 (later):** Add an `annotations` field to step.image that triggers runtime annotation via existing `annotateImage()` function.

**I prefer Phase 1 only** — ship the static library first, add annotation as a follow-up.

## What I Need From You

Design a concrete implementation plan for Phase 1 (static images only). Cover:

1. **File structure** — where images live, what JSON registry looks like
2. **Schema changes** — exact modifications to `create_guide` Zod schema in pcpalTools.js
3. **Server changes** — how the step.image gets expanded to {id, url, alt} before sending to client
4. **Prompt changes** — how `skillMatcher` injects available image IDs into system prompt. What's the injection format?
5. **Client changes** — exact JSX additions to `CommandGuide.jsx` to render the image per step. How does it degrade gracefully if no image?
6. **Graceful fallback** — what happens when agent references an unknown image ID? (Best: silently drop that image but keep the step text.)
7. **A starter set of image IDs** — propose 20 IDs covering email, video call, messaging, browser, Windows, Mac (generic system UI). I'll source the actual images myself.
8. **Verification plan** — how to test manually and what tests to add

Be specific with file paths and line numbers where code changes go. Think about making this MAINTAINABLE — the registry must be easy for a non-developer teammate to populate with new images later.

Length: target ~500-700 words. Clear and actionable.

Even with plain-language descriptions, elderly users still get stuck identifying the exact button on screen. Adding a small reference image per step ("this is what the Compose button looks like") dramatically reduces confusion — this was confirmed in test 3 where Jack got stuck finding the Compose button despite good text directions. The infrastructure is already mostly in place: - `imageAnnotator.js` exists and can draw labeled illustrations via @napi-rs/canvas - `skillImages.js` has an image-per-skill API, but is empty - `/images` Express route already serves `server/assets/annotated/` - Artifact flow (MCP tool → module var → orchestrator → WebSocket → client) is battle-tested This plan adds a generic reference library that works across all 28 skills (email, video calls, messaging, browser, Wi-Fi, etc.) — not email-specific. --- ## Design Decisions (approved) 1. **Agent references images by ID** via a new `image_id` field in `create_guide` step schema 2. **Available IDs are injected into the system prompt conditionally** — only when a matching skill is active, so the prompt stays lean 3. **IDs are decoupled from disk layout** via a JS registry module 4. **Placeholder images generated now** — Claude draws simple labeled illustrations using the existing `imageAnnotator.js`. User replaces with real screenshots later. 5. **Both orchestrators supported** — `agentSdkOrchestrator.js` (primary) and `agentOrchestrator.js` (fallback) 6. **Phase 1 only** — static images. Runtime annotation (arrows, circles) deferred. --- ## File Structure ``` server/assets/ui-references/ NEW folder ├── email/ (placeholder PNGs; user replaces) │ ├── yahoo-compose-button.png │ ├── gmail-compose-button.png │ ├── email-to-field.png │ ├── email-subject-field.png │ └── email-send-button.png ├── video-call/ │ ├── zoom-join-meeting.png │ ├── facetime-call-button.png │ └── mute-microphone-icon.png ├── messaging/ │ ├── imessage-new-message.png │ └── sms-send-arrow.png ├── browser/ │ ├── chrome-address-bar.png │ ├── browser-back-button.png │ └── browser-bookmark-star.png ├── system-windows/ │ ├── windows-start-button.png │ ├── windows-taskbar.png │ ├── windows-wifi-icon.png │ └── windows-settings-gear.png └── system-mac/ ├── mac-apple-menu.png ├── mac-dock.png └── mac-wifi-menubar.png ``` ## Files to Modify/Create ### NEW: `server/core/uiReferenceLibrary.js` Single JS module containing the registry. Exports: - `LIBRARY` — `{id: {file, alt, category, skills[]}}` map - `getById(id)` → `{id, url, alt}` or `null` - `getIdsForSkill(skillId)` → array of IDs - `validateLibrary()` — logs warnings at boot for missing files ### NEW: `server/core/placeholderImageGenerator.js` One-off script using existing `imageAnnotator.js` primitives to generate 20 placeholder PNGs (simple labeled rectangles with target element name + surrounding context hint). Unknown IDs silently dropped.' ), })), ``` In the tool handler (line 521-530), expand `image_id` → full `{id, url, alt}` object before storing in `_lastGuide`. Log and drop unknown IDs. ### MODIFY: `server/core/agentOrchestrator.js` (fallback) Find the local `create_guide`-equivalent tool definition and make the same schema + handler changes. Share the expansion logic by requiring `uiReferenceLibrary`. ### MODIFY: `server/core/skillMatcher.js` Add `buildSkillImagePrompt(skillId)` — returns string like: ``` AVAILABLE UI REFERENCES (use as image_id in create_guide steps): - "yahoo-compose-button": Yellow Compose button, upper-left of Yahoo Mail - ... Only use these exact IDs. If none match, omit image_id. ``` ### MODIFY: `server/core/agentSdkOrchestrator.js` (~line 180) Call `skillMatcher.buildSkillImagePrompt(matchedSkillId)` and append result to the system prompt after the matched skill prompt. ### MODIFY: `server/core/agentOrchestrator.js` (fallback orchestrator) Same prompt injection as primary. ### MODIFY: `client/src/components/Chat/CommandGuide.jsx` Render `step.image` per step: a `

Adding a small reference image per step ("this is what the Compose button looks like") dramatically reduces confusion — this was confirmed in test 3 where Jack got stuck finding the Compose button despite good text directions. The infrastructure is already mostly in place: - `imageAnnotator.js` exists and can draw labeled illustrations via @napi-rs/canvas - `skillImages.js` has an image-per-skill API, but is empty - `/images` Express route already serves `server/assets/annotated/` - Artifact flow (MCP tool → module var → orchestrator → WebSocket → client) is battle-tested This plan adds a generic reference library that works across all 28 skills (email, video calls, messaging, browser, Wi-Fi, etc.) — not email-specific. --- ## Design Decisions (approved) 1. **Agent references images by ID** via a new `image_id` field in `create_guide` step schema 2. **Available IDs are injected into the system prompt conditionally** — only when a matching skill is active, so the prompt stays lean 3. **IDs are decoupled from disk layout** via a JS registry module 4. **Placeholder images generated now** — Claude draws simple labeled illustrations using the existing `imageAnnotator.js`. User replaces with real screenshots later. 5. **Both orchestrators supported** — `agentSdkOrchestrator.js` (primary) and `agentOrchestrator.js` (fallback) 6. **Phase 1 only** — static images. Runtime annotation (arrows, circles) deferred. --- ## File Structure ``` server/assets/ui-references/ NEW folder ├── email/ (placeholder PNGs; user replaces) │ ├── yahoo-compose-button.png │ ├── gmail-compose-button.png │ ├── email-to-field.png │ ├── email-subject-field.png │ └── email-send-button.png ├── video-call/ │ ├── zoom-join-meeting.png │ ├── facetime-call-button.png │ └── mute-microphone-icon.png ├── messaging/ │ ├── imessage-new-message.png │ └── sms-send-arrow.png ├── browser/ │ ├── chrome-address-bar.png │ ├── browser-back-button.png │ └── browser-bookmark-star.png ├── system-windows/ │ ├── windows-start-button.png │ ├── windows-taskbar.png │ ├── windows-wifi-icon.png │ └── windows-settings-gear.png └── system-mac/ ├── mac-apple-menu.png ├── mac-dock.png └── mac-wifi-menubar.png ``` ## Files to Modify/Create ### NEW: `server/core/uiReferenceLibrary.js` Single JS module containing the registry. # Plan: Goal-First Conversation Flow for PC Pal

## Context

When a user says "I want to send an email to my son," the agent immediately jumps to navigation steps ("open your browser," "find the email icon") without first asking which email provider they use or what they want to say. The user's actual goal — writing and sending a message to their son — gets lost in click-by-click instructions. This is the #1 source of frustration for elderly users.

**Root cause:** Neither the system prompt nor the skill definitions instruct the agent to pause and gather context before navigating. The `send-email` skill prompt says *"Walk them through opening their email app"* — which triggers immediate step-giving.

**Fix:** Add a mandatory "Goal-First Conversation Flow" section to both orchestrators' system prompts, and update communication skill definitions to match.

---

## Files to Modify (5 files)

### 1. `server/core/agentOrchestrator.js` — Insert Goal-First rules into `buildSystemPrompt()`

**Where:** Line 358, between `${confusionNote}` and `## Comfort-Level Guidelines`

Insert this new section:

```
## GOAL-FIRST CONVERSATION FLOW (follow this before all other rules)

When the user states a goal (sending an email, making a video call, writing a message, printing something, etc.), you MUST follow this sequence. Do NOT skip ahead to navigation steps.

### Step 1: Acknowledge the goal warmly
Name what the user wants to accomplish. Make it feel achievable.
Example: "Sending an email to your son — what a lovely idea! Let's make that happen together."

### Step 2: Gather missing context BEFORE giving any navigation steps
Ask for the information you need to actually help. Do NOT start with "open your browser" or "find the icon."

For email tasks: which email service (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo) and what they want to say.
For video calls: which app (FaceTime, Zoom) and who they want to call.
For messages: which app and who the recipient is.

If memory already tells you their email provider or app, skip that question — ask for the next missing piece.
Ask ONE clear question at the end of your response.

### Step 3: Keep the end goal visible in EVERY response
Thread their goal into each step.
BAD: "Now click the compose button."
GOOD: "Now let's start writing that email to your son — look for a button that says Compose."

### Step 4: Offer to draft content when you have enough context
Once you know what they want to say and who it is for, offer to write it:
"Would you like me to suggest what to write? You can change anything."
This is often MORE helpful than navigation — elderly users struggle with WHAT to type, not just WHERE to click.

### Step 5: Remember preferences for next time
After learning their email provider or app preference, save it using save_note_for_user so you never ask again.

IMPORTANT: A response that jumps straight to "open your browser" without knowing the user's email provider is WRONG. Context first, navigation second.
```

---

### 2. `server/core/agentSdkOrchestrator.js` — Insert Goal-First rules into `buildSystemPrompt()`

**Where:** Line 59, between the memory summary block and `## GROUNDING RULES`

Insert the same Goal-First section, but adapted for this orchestrator's shorter style and using `save_memory` instead of `save_note_for_user`:

```
## GOAL-FIRST CONVERSATION FLOW (follow this before all other rules)

When the user states a goal (sending email, video call, writing a message, printing, etc.), follow this sequence strictly:

1. **Acknowledge** their goal warmly. Make it feel achievable.
2. **Gather context** BEFORE any navigation. Ask which app/service they use, what they want to say, who the recipient is. If memory already has this, skip to the next missing piece. Ask ONE question at a time.
3. **Keep the goal visible** in every response. Thread it into steps: "To send that email to your son, look for the Compose button."
4. **Offer to draft content** once you have enough info: "Want me to suggest what to write? You can change anything."
5. **Save preferences** via save_memory (type: context) so you never ask the same question twice.

A response that jumps to "open your browser" without knowing the user's email provider is WRONG. Context first, navigation second.
```

---

### 3. `server/core/sharedConstants.js` — Reinforce in comfort level 1-2

**Where:** Line 59, add one line to the level 1-2 return value

```javascript
if (level <= 1) {
    return `BRAND NEW to computers.
- Use everyday analogies (folder = filing cabinet drawer)
- Maximum 2 steps per guide, then wait for "done" before continuing
- Use create_guide for any multi-step task
- After each step, ask "Did that work?"
- For goal tasks (email, call, message): ask what app they use and what they want to say BEFORE giving steps`;
  }
```

---

### 4. `server/skills/send-email.json` — Rewrite prompt to context-first

Replace the `prompt` field:

```json
"prompt": "The user wants to send an email. FIRST ask which email service they use (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, AOL) if not already known from memory. Ask what they want to say and if they know the recipient's email address. Once you have the provider and recipient, THEN guide them step by step through opening the app, composing, and sending. After they reach the compose screen, offer to draft the message for them. Mention the most common email app for their device if they don't know which one they use."
```

### 5. `server/skills/text-message.json` — Rewrite prompt to context-first

Replace the `prompt` field:

```json
"prompt": "The user wants to send a text message. FIRST ask who they want to message and whether they have the person's phone number. Once you know the recipient, THEN guide them through opening the Messages app, starting a new conversation, and sending. Offer to help compose the message if they want. Mention the difference between green (SMS) and blue (iMessage) bubbles on iPhone if relevant."
```

### (Optional) `server/skills/video-call.json` — Already partially context-first, strengthen it

Replace the `prompt` field:

```json
"prompt": "The user wants to make a video call. FIRST ask which app they use (FaceTime, Zoom, Google Meet, Teams, Skype) if not known from memory, and who they want to call. For iPhone suggest FaceTime, for others suggest Zoom. Once you know the app and recipient, THEN guide them through opening the app, starting a call, and making sure camera and microphone are on. Reassure them it is normal to feel nervous the first time."
```

---

## What stays the same

- All 26 existing tools — untouched
- Safety monitor / scam detection — untouched
- Vocabulary filter — untouched
- Visual guides / step sequences — untouched
- Confusion Escalation Ladder — compatible (activates during steps, which come after context-gathering)
- Atomic Steps / Working Memory Cap / Never Rush — compatible (govern HOW steps are given, not WHEN)
- Grounding rules in agentSdkOrchestrator — untouched, no conflict

---

## Verification

1. **Manual test** — Send these messages and verify the agent asks for context before giving navigation:
   - "I want to send an email to my son"
   - "I need to video call my doctor"  
   - "How do I text my granddaughter"
   
2. **Check for each:** (a) Goal acknowledged, (b) Context question asked, (c) NO navigation steps in first response

3. **Run existing tests** — `npm test` to confirm nothing breaks

4. **Test memory integration** — After telling the agent "I use Yahoo," verify subsequent conversations don't re-ask

---

## Implementation order

1. `sharedConstants.js` — one-line addition (lowest risk)
2. `send-email.json`, `text-message.json`, `video-call.json` — skill prompt rewrites
3. `agentOrchestrator.js` — insert Goal-First section at line 358
4. `agentSdkOrchestrator.js` — insert Goal-First section at line 59

Great catch! The feature is working but the agent isn't using it. Let me diagnose and explain, then propose the fix.

---

## Why Images Didn't Appear

### Root Cause 1: Skill-to-Image Mappings Are Too Narrow

Looking at `video-call` in the registry, it only maps to 3 images:
- `zoom-join-meeting` (only useful AFTER Zoom is installed)
- `facetime-call-button`
- `mute-microphone-icon`

But the agent's video-call guide talked about things like:
- "Open your internet app" → would need **Chrome icon** (doesn't exist!)
- "Click in the long white box at the top" → would need `chrome-address-bar` — **but that's only mapped to browser/email skills**, not video-call
- "Get Zoom" → would need a **Zoom download button** image (doesn't exist!)

The registry doesn't have the right images, and the ones it has aren't mapped to video-call.

### Root Cause 2: Skill Matching Is Per-Message, Not Sticky

Turn 3 was *"yes its Fred"*. That message has zero video-call triggers, so the skill matcher returned **nothing**, which means **zero image IDs were injected into the prompt** for that response — even though the conversation was still about video calling. The agent couldn't use `zoom-join-meeting` because it didn't know it existed.

### Root Cause 3: Prompt Is Too Passive

My current prompt says:
> *"When writing a guide step that mentions a button or icon listed above, add image_id..."*

This is optional-sounding. The agent treats it as a nice-to-have. Should be:
> *"You MUST add image_id to EVERY step that mentions an element listed above. This is the single most impactful thing you can do to help elderly users — a picture is worth a thousand words to someone who can't visualize UI elements."*

---

## Proposed Fix (4 parts)

1. **Add 7-10 missing images** — the ones the agent actually wants:
   - `chrome-icon`, `edge-icon`, `firefox-icon`, `safari-icon` (the app icons themselves)
   - `zoom-download-button`, `zoom-homepage`
   - `zoom-app-icon` (after install, on desktop)

2. **Broaden skill mappings** — system UI images (taskbar, start button, dock, wifi) should map to MANY skills because elderly users always start at the taskbar/desktop. Browser images should map to everything that goes online (video-call, send-email, browser, settings, etc.)

3. **Sticky skill matching** — if the current message doesn't match a skill but the previous assistant turn had a matched skill, reuse that skill's image IDs. This keeps the agent equipped with images throughout a multi-turn conversation.

4. **Strengthen the prompt** — make image use mandatory, not optional. Add an explicit line: *"If a guide step mentions an element listed in AVAILABLE UI REFERENCES and you don't include image_id, you have failed the user."*

---

# Plan: Make the Agent Actually USE the Image Library

## Context

The image library shipped (commit `3f181b1`), but test 4 revealed the agent isn't using it. When guiding Jack through a Zoom video call, the side-panel guides showed only text ("colorful circle", "long white box at the top") — no `image_id` was included in any guide step.

**Three root causes identified from test 4:**

1. **Library gaps** — agent wanted to show "Chrome icon" and "Zoom download" but these images don't exist in the registry. For example, the `video-call` skill only has 3 images (zoom-join-meeting, facetime-call-button, mute-microphone-icon), none of which are useful for the early "open internet app → go to zoom.us" phase.

2. **Per-message skill matching** — the image prompt injection only happens when the current message matches a skill. But "yes its Fred" (turn 3) doesn't trigger video-call triggers, so the agent received ZERO image IDs for that response — even though the conversation was clearly still about video-calling.

3. **Passive prompt** — the current instruction says "add image_id when relevant" which the agent treats as optional. Needs to be directive/mandatory.

---

## Fix (4 parts)

### Part 1: Add 8 missing images to `uiReferenceLibrary.js`

New entries (placeholder generator auto-creates PNGs at next startup):

| ID | File | Alt | Skills |
|----|------|-----|--------|
| `chrome-icon` | `browser/chrome-icon.png` | Chrome browser icon — colorful circle (red, yellow, green, blue) | `*` |
| `edge-icon` | `browser/edge-icon.png` | Microsoft Edge icon — blue and green swirl | `*` |
| `firefox-icon` | `browser/firefox-icon.png` | Firefox icon — orange fox wrapped around a blue globe | `*` |
| `safari-icon` | `browser/safari-icon.png` | Safari icon — blue compass | `*` |
| `zoom-download-button` | `video-call/zoom-download-button.png` | Blue "Download" button on zoom.us website | `video-call` |
| `zoom-homepage` | `video-call/zoom-homepage.png` | Zoom.us homepage with the Download button visible | `video-call` |
| `zoom-app-icon` | `video-call/zoom-app-icon.png` | Zoom desktop app icon — blue with white video camera | `video-call` |
| `outlook-app-icon` | `email/outlook-app-icon.png` | Outlook desktop app icon — blue with white envelope and 'O' | `send-email` |

### Part 2: Introduce `'*'` wildcard + broaden existing skill mappings

**In `uiReferenceLibrary.js`:**

Support `skills: ['*']` meaning "always available". Update `getIdsForSkill(skillId)` to include entries where `skills` contains `'*'` OR the target skillId.

**Promote these foundational images to `'*'`:**
- `chrome-address-bar` → `'*'` (every task that goes online needs the address bar)
- `windows-taskbar` → `'*'`
- `mac-dock` → `'*'`
- `windows-start-button` → `'*'`
- `mac-apple-menu` → `'*'`

This means: whenever ANY skill matches, these foundational images are always in scope. Cleanly solves the "foundational images aren't mapped to every skill" problem without massive list maintenance.

### Part 3: Sticky skill matching in `agentSdkOrchestrator.js`

After calling `matchSkill(text)`, if it returns null AND there are prior user messages in the conversation, walk backwards through the last 5 user messages and reuse the first match found. This keeps the agent equipped with image IDs throughout a multi-turn conversation even when intermediate turns ("yes", "done", "Fred") don't have skill triggers.

Inline in `processMessage()` around line 179:
```js
let skillMatch = skillMatcher.matchSkill(text);
if (!skillMatch) {
  const recentUserMessages = dbMessages.filter(m => m.role === 'user').slice(-5);
  for (let i = recentUserMessages.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
    const prev = skillMatcher.matchSkill(recentUserMessages[i].body);
    if (prev) {
      skillMatch = prev;
      console.log(`[agentSdkOrchestrator] Sticky skill: "${prev.skill.name}" (from earlier turn)`);
      break;
    }
  }
}
```

### Part 4: Strengthen the prompt in `skillMatcher.buildSkillImagePrompt()`

Replace the passive "when relevant, add image_id" with a directive tone. New version:

```
## AVAILABLE UI REFERENCES (pictures the user can see)

CRITICAL: Pictures help elderly users more than any amount of text description. For EVERY guide step that mentions an element listed below, you MUST include "image_id": "<exact-id>" so the user sees a picture of what you're describing. A step that says "click the colorful circle" WITHOUT image_id="chrome-icon" has failed the user.

Available images:
  - "chrome-icon": Chrome browser icon — colorful circle (red, yellow, green, blue)
  - "yahoo-compose-button": Yellow Compose button, upper-left of Yahoo Mail
  ...

Rules:
- Include image_id on every step describing a listed element
- Use the EXACT id string — no variations, no new ids
- If no id matches the element, omit image_id (never invent)
```

---

## Files to Modify

| File | What |
|------|------|
| `server/core/uiReferenceLibrary.js` | Add 8 new entries + promote 5 to `'*'` + update `getIdsForSkill` for wildcard |
| `server/core/skillMatcher.js` | Rewrite `buildSkillImagePrompt()` header to be directive |
| `server/core/agentSdkOrchestrator.js` | Add sticky skill match fallback around line 179 |

`placeholderImageGenerator.js` needs NO change — it iterates the registry and auto-creates placeholders for new entries on next server startup.

---

## Verification

1. **Restart server** — confirm logs show: `[placeholderImageGenerator] Generated 8 placeholder(s)` and `[uiReferenceLibrary] 28/28 references valid`.
2. **Test the same video-call flow** — expected:
   - Turn 1 ("I want to video call my son"): guide steps include `image_id: "chrome-icon"` for "open internet app" and `image_id: "chrome-address-bar"` for "type zoom.us"
   - Turn 3 ("yes its Fred"): sticky match keeps video-call active → agent still has Zoom + browser images available
   - Later: `image_id: "zoom-download-button"` when agent says "click Download"
3. **Manual prompt check** — trigger a `scam-check` query. Confirm the `AVAILABLE UI REFERENCES` section is still injected (because `'*'` images apply) and is shorter (no email/video-call images).
4. **Tests** — `npm test` → all 169 must still pass. No new tests required (this is a data/prompt change, not new logic).

# Plan: Make the Agent Actually USE the Image Library

## Context

The image library shipped (commit `3f181b1`), but test 4 revealed the agent isn't using it. When guiding Jack through a Zoom video call, the side-panel guides showed only text ("colorful circle", "long white box at the top") — no `image_id` was included in any guide step.

**Three root causes identified from test 4:**

1. **Library gaps** — agent wanted to show "Chrome icon" and "Zoom download" but these images don't exist in the registry. For example, the `video-call` skill only has 3 images (zoom-join-meeting, facetime-call-button, mute-microphone-icon), none of which are useful for the early "open internet app → go to zoom.us" phase.

2. **Per-message skill matching** — the image prompt injection only happens when the current message matches a skill. But "yes its Fred" (turn 3) doesn't trigger video-call triggers, so the agent received ZERO image IDs for that response — even though the conversation was clearly still about video-calling.

3. **Passive prompt** — the current instruction says "add image_id when relevant" which the agent treats as optional. Needs to be directive/mandatory.

---

## Fix (4 parts)

### Part 1: Add 8 missing images to `uiReferenceLibrary.js`

New entries (placeholder generator auto-creates PNGs at next startup):

| ID | File | Alt | Skills |
|----|------|-----|--------|
| `chrome-icon` | `browser/chrome-icon.png` | Chrome browser icon — colorful circle (red, yellow, green, blue) | `*` |
| `edge-icon` | `browser/edge-icon.png` | Microsoft Edge icon — blue and green swirl | `*` |
| `firefox-icon` | `browser/firefox-icon.png` | Firefox icon — orange fox wrapped around a blue globe | `*` |
| `safari-icon` | `browser/safari-icon.png` | Safari icon — blue compass | `*` |
| `zoom-download-button` | `video-call/zoom-download-button.png` | Blue "Download" button on zoom.us website | `video-call` |
| `zoom-homepage` | `video-call/zoom-homepage.png` | Zoom.us homepage with the Download button visible | `video-call` |
| `zoom-app-icon` | `video-call/zoom-app-icon.png` | Zoom desktop app icon — blue with white video camera | `video-call` |
| `outlook-app-icon` | `email/outlook-app-icon.png` | Outlook desktop app icon — blue with white envelope and 'O' | `send-email` |

### Part 2: Introduce `'*'` wildcard + broaden existing skill mappings

**In `uiReferenceLibrary.js`:**

Support `skills: ['*']` meaning "always available". Update `getIdsForSkill(skillId)` to include entries where `skills` contains `'*'` OR the target skillId.

**Promote these foundational images to `'*'`:**
- `chrome-address-bar` → `'*'` (every task that goes online needs the address bar)
- `windows-taskbar` → `'*'`
- `mac-dock` → `'*'`
- `windows-start-button` → `'*'`
- `mac-apple-menu` → `'*'`

This means: whenever ANY skill matches, these foundational images are always in scope. Cleanly solves the "foundational images aren't mapped to every skill" problem without massive list maintenance.

### Part 3: Sticky skill matching in `agentSdkOrchestrator.js`

After calling `matchSkill(text)`, if it returns null AND there are prior user messages in the conversation, walk backwards through the last 5 user messages and reuse the first match found. This keeps the agent equipped with image IDs throughout a multi-turn conversation even when intermediate turns ("yes", "done", "Fred") don't have skill triggers.

Inline in `processMessage()` around line 179:
```js
let skillMatch = skillMatcher.matchSkill(text);
if (!skillMatch) {
  const recentUserMessages = dbMessages.filter(m => m.role === 'user').slice(-5);
  for (let i = recentUserMessages.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
    const prev = skillMatcher.matchSkill(recentUserMessages[i].body);
    if (prev) {
      skillMatch = prev;
      console.log(`[agentSdkOrchestrator] Sticky skill: "${prev.skill.name}" (from earlier turn)`);
      break;
    }
  }
}
```

### Part 4: Strengthen the prompt in `skillMatcher.buildSkillImagePrompt()`

Replace the passive "when relevant, add image_id" with a directive tone. New version:

```
## AVAILABLE UI REFERENCES (pictures the user can see)

CRITICAL: Pictures help elderly users more than any amount of text description. For EVERY guide step that mentions an element listed below, you MUST include "image_id": "<exact-id>" so the user sees a picture of what you're describing. A step that says "click the colorful circle" WITHOUT image_id="chrome-icon" has failed the user.

Available images:
  - "chrome-icon": Chrome browser icon — colorful circle (red, yellow, green, blue)
  - "yahoo-compose-button": Yellow Compose button, upper-left of Yahoo Mail
  ...

Rules:
- Include image_id on every step describing a listed element
- Use the EXACT id string — no variations, no new ids
- If no id matches the element, omit image_id (never invent)
```

---

## Files to Modify

| File | What |
|------|------|
| `server/core/uiReferenceLibrary.js` | Add 8 new entries + promote 5 to `'*'` + update `getIdsForSkill` for wildcard |
| `server/core/skillMatcher.js` | Rewrite `buildSkillImagePrompt()` header to be directive |
| `server/core/agentSdkOrchestrator.js` | Add sticky skill match fallback around line 179 |

`placeholderImageGenerator.js` needs NO change — it iterates the registry and auto-creates placeholders for new entries on next server startup.

---

## Verification

1. **Restart server** — confirm logs show: `[placeholderImageGenerator] Generated 8 placeholder(s)` and `[uiReferenceLibrary] 28/28 references valid`.
2. **Test the same video-call flow** — expected:
   - Turn 1 ("I want to video call my son"): guide steps include `image_id: "chrome-icon"` for "open internet app" and `image_id: "chrome-address-bar"` for "type zoom.us"
   - Turn 3 ("yes its Fred"): sticky match keeps video-call active → agent still has Zoom + browser images available
   - Later: `image_id: "zoom-download-button"` when agent says "click Download"
3. **Manual prompt check** — trigger a `scam-check` query. Confirm the `AVAILABLE UI REFERENCES` section is still injected (because `'*'` images apply) and is shorter (no email/video-call images).
4. **Tests** — `npm test` → all 169 must still pass. No new tests required (this is a data/prompt change, not new logic).

  // Detect conversation phase: opening, mid-conversation, or follow-up

2. **Gather context** BEFORE any navigation. Ask which app/service they use, what they want to say, who the recipient is. If memory already has this, skip to the next missing piece. Ask ONE question at a time.

If the user's device doesn't match what diagnostic tools report (e.g., user says Android but tools show macOS), the tools are reading the SERVER, not the user's device. In that case, give instructions based on what the USER told you, not tool output. Say "Based on your ${user?.os_type || 'device'}..." and ignore contradictory tool data.

---

## 🎯 Critical Fix

The actual bug was **not in the agent's behavior** — it was in the **Vite dev server proxy**. Images were never reaching the browser because port 5173 didn't know to forward `/ui-references` requests to port 3001 where the backend serves the files.

---

## How to Test (Final Time)

This is important — Vite loads its config at startup too, so you need to fully restart **both** processes.

### 1. Stop the current server
```
Ctrl + C
```

### 2. Pull the latest changes
```bash
git pull
```

### 3. Start fresh (loads new Vite config + server code)
```bash
npm run dev
```

### 4. Hard-refresh browser
```
Ctrl + F5
```
at http://localhost:5173

### 5. Start a new chat and type:
```
hi i want to video call my son
```

### 6. Watch TWO places:

**A. The server terminal** — you'll now see diagnostic lines like:
```
[MCP] create_guide called: "Find Your Internet App" — image_ids: [step1=windows-taskbar, step2=chrome-icon, step3=edge-icon]
[MCP]   ✓ Resolved "windows-taskbar" → /ui-references/system-windows/windows-taskbar.png

[MCP]   ✓ Resolved "edge-icon" → /ui-references/browser/edge-icon.png
[MCP] Guide finalized: "Find Your Internet App" (3 steps, 3 with images)
```

**B. The browser** — the side-panel guide should now show placeholder images under each step.

### 7. Share what you see

If you see IDs in the log but no images → browser/network issue (open DevTools Network tab, look for failed `/ui-references/*` requests)

If you see `image_ids: [step1=NONE, step2=NONE, ...]` in the log → agent still isn't using image_id (prompt problem, we'll dig deeper)

If you see images both in logs AND browser → 🎉 we're done!

## 🔍 Small Things I Still See

### Minor Issue 1: One step missed an image

In the "Open Zoom for Your Video Call" guide, step 2 says *"If you see the Zoom little picture in the taskbar, click it twice quickly..."* — this mentions the Zoom icon but has no `image_id`. The agent should have added `image_id="zoom-app-icon"` here too. Not a bug — just an inconsistency that'll improve as the model internalizes the pattern.

### Minor Issue 2: "save from the internet" sounds awkward

I noticed this phrase: *"we just need to **save from the internet** it first"*. This is your vocabulary filter replacing "download" → "save from the internet" (which is in `basicSubstitutions.json`). It was a reasonable substitution in theory but reads oddly in practice — especially the word order "save from the internet it".

**Easy fix:** Change the substitution from `"save from the internet"` to just `"download"` (keep the word — it's well-known enough) or `"save to your computer"` (cleaner phrasing).

### Minor Issue 3: A leftover filter split

I spotted *"it's reliable. And fairly easy to use."* — the filter split at "and". The original was probably "it's reliable and fairly easy to use" (21 words in its full parent sentence). My 4-word minimum allows this split because both sides qualify, but "fairly easy to use" as its own sentence still sounds clipped.

**Possible fix:** Bump the minimum from 4 to 6 words per segment. Would reduce over-splitting at the cost of keeping a few long sentences intact.

# Plan: Make the Agent Actually USE the Image Library

## Context

The image library shipped (commit `3f181b1`), but test 4 revealed the agent isn't using it. When guiding Jack through a Zoom video call, the side-panel guides showed only text ("colorful circle", "long white box at the top") — no `image_id` was included in any guide step.

**Three root causes identified from test 4:**

1. **Library gaps** — agent wanted to show "Chrome icon" and "Zoom download" but these images don't exist in the registry. For example, the `video-call` skill only has 3 images (zoom-join-meeting, facetime-call-button, mute-microphone-icon), none of which are useful for the early "open internet app → go to zoom.us" phase.

2. **Per-message skill matching** — the image prompt injection only happens when the current message matches a skill. But "yes its Fred" (turn 3) doesn't trigger video-call triggers, so the agent received ZERO image IDs for that response — even though the conversation was clearly still about video-calling.

3. **Passive prompt** — the current instruction says "add image_id when relevant" which the agent treats as optional. Needs to be directive/mandatory.

---

## Fix (4 parts)

### Part 1: Add 8 missing images to `uiReferenceLibrary.js`

New entries (placeholder generator auto-creates PNGs at next startup):

| ID | File | Alt | Skills |
|----|------|-----|--------|
| `chrome-icon` | `browser/chrome-icon.png` | Chrome browser icon — colorful circle (red, yellow, green, blue) | `*` |
| `edge-icon` | `browser/edge-icon.png` | Microsoft Edge icon — blue and green swirl | `*` |
| `firefox-icon` | `browser/firefox-icon.png` | Firefox icon — orange fox wrapped around a blue globe | `*` |
| `safari-icon` | `browser/safari-icon.png` | Safari icon — blue compass | `*` |
| `zoom-download-button` | `video-call/zoom-download-button.png` | Blue "Download" button on zoom.us website | `video-call` |
| `zoom-homepage` | `video-call/zoom-homepage.png` | Zoom.us homepage with the Download button visible | `video-call` |
| `zoom-app-icon` | `video-call/zoom-app-icon.png` | Zoom desktop app icon — blue with white video camera | `video-call` |
| `outlook-app-icon` | `email/outlook-app-icon.png` | Outlook desktop app icon — blue with white envelope and 'O' | `send-email` |

### Part 2: Introduce `'*'` wildcard + broaden existing skill mappings

**In `uiReferenceLibrary.js`:**

Support `skills: ['*']` meaning "always available". Update `getIdsForSkill(skillId)` to include entries where `skills` contains `'*'` OR the target skillId.

**Promote these foundational images to `'*'`:**
- `chrome-address-bar` → `'*'` (every task that goes online needs the address bar)
- `windows-taskbar` → `'*'`
- `mac-dock` → `'*'`
- `windows-start-button` → `'*'`
- `mac-apple-menu` → `'*'`

This means: whenever ANY skill matches, these foundational images are always in scope. Cleanly solves the "foundational images aren't mapped to every skill" problem without massive list maintenance.

### Part 3: Sticky skill matching in `agentSdkOrchestrator.js`

After calling `matchSkill(text)`, if it returns null AND there are prior user messages in the conversation, walk backwards through the last 5 user messages and reuse the first match found. This keeps the agent equipped with image IDs throughout a multi-turn conversation even when intermediate turns ("yes", "done", "Fred") don't have skill triggers.

Inline in `processMessage()` around line 179:
```js
let skillMatch = skillMatcher.matchSkill(text);
if (!skillMatch) {
  const recentUserMessages = dbMessages.filter(m => m.role === 'user').slice(-5);
  for (let i = recentUserMessages.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
    const prev = skillMatcher.matchSkill(recentUserMessages[i].body);
    if (prev) {
      skillMatch = prev;
      console.log(`[agentSdkOrchestrator] Sticky skill: "${prev.skill.name}" (from earlier turn)`);
      break;
    }
  }
}
```

### Part 4: Strengthen the prompt in `skillMatcher.buildSkillImagePrompt()`

Replace the passive "when relevant, add image_id" with a directive tone. New version:

```
## AVAILABLE UI REFERENCES (pictures the user can see)

CRITICAL: Pictures help elderly users more than any amount of text description. For EVERY guide step that mentions an element listed below, you MUST include "image_id": "<exact-id>" so the user sees a picture of what you're describing. A step that says "click the colorful circle" WITHOUT image_id="chrome-icon" has failed the user.

Available images:
  - "chrome-icon": Chrome browser icon — colorful circle (red, yellow, green, blue)
  - "yahoo-compose-button": Yellow Compose button, upper-left of Yahoo Mail
  ...

Rules:
- Include image_id on every step describing a listed element
- Use the EXACT id string — no variations, no new ids
- If no id matches the element, omit image_id (never invent)
```

---

## Files to Modify

| File | What |
|------|------|
| `server/core/uiReferenceLibrary.js` | Add 8 new entries + promote 5 to `'*'` + update `getIdsForSkill` for wildcard |
| `server/core/skillMatcher.js` | Rewrite `buildSkillImagePrompt()` header to be directive |
| `server/core/agentSdkOrchestrator.js` | Add sticky skill match fallback around line 179 |

`placeholderImageGenerator.js` needs NO change — it iterates the registry and auto-creates placeholders for new entries on next server startup.

---

## Verification

1. **Restart server** — confirm logs show: `[placeholderImageGenerator] Generated 8 placeholder(s)` and `[uiReferenceLibrary] 28/28 references valid`.
2. **Test the same video-call flow** — expected:
   - Turn 1 ("I want to video call my son"): guide steps include `image_id: "chrome-icon"` for "open internet app" and `image_id: "chrome-address-bar"` for "type zoom.us"
   - Turn 3 ("yes its Fred"): sticky match keeps video-call active → agent still has Zoom + browser images available
   - Later: `image_id: "zoom-download-button"` when agent says "click Download"
3. **Manual prompt check** — trigger a `scam-check` query. Confirm the `AVAILABLE UI REFERENCES` section is still injected (because `'*'` images apply) and is shorter (no email/video-call images).
4. **Tests** — `npm test` → all 169 must still pass. No new tests required (this is a data/prompt change, not new logic).

content.text:
**PR for review — strongly recommended.** Your teammates haven't seen any of this work, and it's substantial: system prompt changes, new image pipeline, 26 new assets, skill rewrites. Landing it cold on main would surprise them.

**On reversibility:**
- **Yes, reversible** — `git revert <merge-commit>` creates a new commit that undoes a merge. Nothing is ever "lost" in git history.
- **BUT**: once teammates merge their own work on top of a merged main, reverting gets messier (potential conflicts with later work). The longer it sits, the more annoying to back out.
- **Force-pushing to main to wipe the merge** is technically possible but destructive and would break everyone's local clones — don't do that.

**Bottom line**: PR costs you maybe a day of waiting for reviews, but it trades that for zero risk of surprising your group. Even if you trust them to love it, they'll appreciate seeing it first.

## Summary

Improves agent behavior for elderly/beginner users across three areas: how it talks, how it shows things, and how reliably its output reads.

**1. Goal-first conversation flow** — Agent now acknowledges the user's stated goal, gathers context BEFORE navigation, and keeps the goal visible across turns. Closed #39.

**2. UI reference image library** — New pipeline that embeds real screenshots (Chrome icon, address bar, Zoom download button, etc.) inside guide steps so users see what they should click. 36 image slots, 26 real screenshots imported from the team lead's desktop; 10 placeholders remain. The agent is now required (not just encouraged) to use `image_id` in every guide step that references a pictured element. Closed #42, #43, #44, #45, #46.

**3. Plain-language enforcement** — Guide step bodies translate every jargon word (no bare "double-click", "browser", "URL" without explanation). Vocabulary filter bugs fixed: trailing-comma artifacts, awkward "so" splits, short-clause fragments, ungrammatical "download" substitution. Closed #40, #41.

**4. Skill rewrites** — `send-email`, `text-message`, `video-call` skills rewritten to push context-gathering before navigation. Closed #47.

**Merged `main` into this branch** (Practice Mode, P2P video, Ollama, find-on-screen, conversation sidebar) — auto-merged cleanly in all 4 overlapping files. All 186 tests pass.

## Files of note

- `server/core/uiReferenceLibrary.js` — new 36-entry registry, wildcard `*` for foundational images
- `server/core/placeholderImageGenerator.js` — auto-generates labeled PNGs for any missing files
- `server/core/agentSdkOrchestrator.js` — goal-first prompt + sticky skill matching across turns
- `server/core/vocabularyFilter.js` — fragment fixes, MIN_WORDS_PER_SEGMENT = 6
- `server/assets/ui-references/**` — 36 PNGs (26 real screenshots, 10 placeholders)
- `client/src/components/Chat/CommandGuide.jsx` + `.css` — renders `step.image` with graceful fallback
- `client/vite.config.js` — added `/ui-references` proxy (was blocking images in dev)

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm test` passes all 186 tests (already green locally)
- [ ] Start `npm run dev`, confirm server logs: `[uiReferenceLibrary] 36/36 references valid`
- [ ] In browser, send "I want to video-call my son" as a beginner-profile user
- [ ] Verify the Chrome/Edge icon appears in the guide step (not just text)
- [ ] Verify agent acknowledges the goal before navigating (no "double-click the browser" cold-open)
- [ ] Verify Practice Mode from `main` still works — unrelated to this branch but worth a smoke-test post-merge

Fixes #39, #40, #41, #42, #43, #44, #45, #46, #47

## Known limitations

- 10 library entries still have placeholders (not blocking — the fallback renders a labeled PNG so the UI doesn't break)
- UI not smoke-tested post-merge — Jest covers the logic but nothing clicked a button in a real browser after pulling in Practice Mode

commit c2926e55bec39994e009280399ce7e4f792408de
Author: Dean Hauser <Deanhauser10@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Apr 21 17:08:08 2026 +0000

    Add email/password accounts with cookie sessions
    
    Users can now register with email and password, log in, and have their
    conversations persisted. Anonymous mode is still available — guest
    users get a session cookie but their chats live in memory only and are
    wiped when the WebSocket disconnects (per "need to be logged in to
    save conversations").
    
    Server
     - users table gains email (case-insensitive unique), password_hash
       (bcryptjs), is_anonymous, training_opt_in. New user_sessions table
       holds server-side revocable tokens.
     - Auth middleware parses the pcpal_session cookie on every request and
       attaches req.user. requireSelf guards all /api/users/:id/* routes.
     - New /api/auth/{register,login,logout,me}. POST /api/users still
       creates anonymous users but now also issues a session cookie.
     - /api/conversations/:id/* now check ownership; /api/quality/* and
       /api/chat derive userId from the session instead of trusting the
       request body.
     - WebSocket init rejects connections whose claimed userId doesn't
       match the session cookie.
     - conversationState transparently routes anonymous users through
       in-memory ephemeral Maps so DB writes are skipped entirely.
    
    Client
     - New AuthScreen (sign in / create account / continue without account)
       gates the app. useUser bootstraps identity from /api/auth/me.
     - OnboardingFlow updates the existing user in place rather than
       always creating a new one.
     - Header exposes a Sign out button and a training-data consent toggle
       (default off, only shown to authenticated users).
    
    Training export
     - scripts/export-training-data.js writes JSONL of completed
       conversations, filtered to users with training_opt_in=1.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

- User's exact words: "Too many words in the response"
- Agent's response included repetitive phrasing ("wireless internet" 7 times in one message)

- Later: User asks "can you help me find this" → Agent again says "Run the commands in the guide above" (same broken reference)

   - Persists across sessions

   - Already injects profile, goals, buddy context, quality tracker state
   - **Blank spot**: No "recent feedback suggestions" section
   - Could add: `const recentSuggestions = ConversationFeedback.getTopRecent(userId, 3); systemPrompt += '\n## Recent Feedback: ' + recentSuggestions`

| Area | Status | Reuse Potential |
|------|--------|-----------------|
| End-of-chat feedback submission | ✅ Complete | High (already working) |
| Per-message quick feedback (thumbs) | ❌ Missing | Must build new |
| Suggestion storage | ✅ Complete | High |
| Suggestion generation (Claude) | ✅ Complete | High |
| **Suggestion retrieval for context** | ❌ **Zero** | Must implement `getTopRecent()` query |
| **Suggestion injection into system prompt** | ❌ **Zero** | Must add to buildSystemPrompt() |
| Admin aggregation/insights | ⚠️ Minimal | Partial (basic stats exist; need parsing) |

---

1. **Add to ConversationFeedback.js**:
   ```javascript
   getTopRecent(userId, limit = 3) {
     return db.prepare(`
       SELECT ai_suggestion, rating, created_at
       FROM conversation_feedback
       WHERE user_id = ? AND ai_suggestion IS NOT NULL
       ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?
     `).all(userId, limit);
   }
   ```

2. **Add to agentOrchestrator.js buildSystemPrompt()**:

This analysis shows a **complete, functioning feedback collection system** with **zero integration back into conversation flow**. The suggestions exist but are invisible to future conversations.

# Plan: Make the Agent Actually USE the Image Library

## Context

The image library shipped (commit `3f181b1`), but test 4 revealed the agent isn't using it. When guiding Jack through a Zoom video call, the side-panel guides showed only text ("colorful circle", "long white box at the top") — no `image_id` was included in any guide step.

**Three root causes identified from test 4:**

1. **Library gaps** — agent wanted to show "Chrome icon" and "Zoom download" but these images don't exist in the registry. For example, the `video-call` skill only has 3 images (zoom-join-meeting, facetime-call-button, mute-microphone-icon), none of which are useful for the early "open internet app → go to zoom.us" phase.

2. **Per-message skill matching** — the image prompt injection only happens when the current message matches a skill. But "yes its Fred" (turn 3) doesn't trigger video-call triggers, so the agent received ZERO image IDs for that response — even though the conversation was clearly still about video-calling.

3. **Passive prompt** — the current instruction says "add image_id when relevant" which the agent treats as optional. Needs to be directive/mandatory.

---

## Fix (4 parts)

### Part 1: Add 8 missing images to `uiReferenceLibrary.js`

New entries (placeholder generator auto-creates PNGs at next startup):

| ID | File | Alt | Skills |
|----|------|-----|--------|
| `chrome-icon` | `browser/chrome-icon.png` | Chrome browser icon — colorful circle (red, yellow, green, blue) | `*` |
| `edge-icon` | `browser/edge-icon.png` | Microsoft Edge icon — blue and green swirl | `*` |
| `firefox-icon` | `browser/firefox-icon.png` | Firefox icon — orange fox wrapped around a blue globe | `*` |
| `safari-icon` | `browser/safari-icon.png` | Safari icon — blue compass | `*` |
| `zoom-download-button` | `video-call/zoom-download-button.png` | Blue "Download" button on zoom.us website | `video-call` |
| `zoom-homepage` | `video-call/zoom-homepage.png` | Zoom.us homepage with the Download button visible | `video-call` |
| `zoom-app-icon` | `video-call/zoom-app-icon.png` | Zoom desktop app icon — blue with white video camera | `video-call` |
| `outlook-app-icon` | `email/outlook-app-icon.png` | Outlook desktop app icon — blue with white envelope and 'O' | `send-email` |

### Part 2: Introduce `'*'` wildcard + broaden existing skill mappings

**In `uiReferenceLibrary.js`:**

Support `skills: ['*']` meaning "always available". Update `getIdsForSkill(skillId)` to include entries where `skills` contains `'*'` OR the target skillId.

**Promote these foundational images to `'*'`:**
- `chrome-address-bar` → `'*'` (every task that goes online needs the address bar)
- `windows-taskbar` → `'*'`
- `mac-dock` → `'*'`
- `windows-start-button` → `'*'`
- `mac-apple-menu` → `'*'`

This means: whenever ANY skill matches, these foundational images are always in scope. Cleanly solves the "foundational images aren't mapped to every skill" problem without massive list maintenance.

### Part 3: Sticky skill matching in `agentSdkOrchestrator.js`

After calling `matchSkill(text)`, if it returns null AND there are prior user messages in the conversation, walk backwards through the last 5 user messages and reuse the first match found. This keeps the agent equipped with image IDs throughout a multi-turn conversation even when intermediate turns ("yes", "done", "Fred") don't have skill triggers.

Inline in `processMessage()` around line 179:
```js
let skillMatch = skillMatcher.matchSkill(text);
if (!skillMatch) {
  const recentUserMessages = dbMessages.filter(m => m.role === 'user').slice(-5);
  for (let i = recentUserMessages.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
    const prev = skillMatcher.matchSkill(recentUserMessages[i].body);
    if (prev) {
      skillMatch = prev;
      console.log(`[agentSdkOrchestrator] Sticky skill: "${prev.skill.name}" (from earlier turn)`);
      break;
    }
  }
}
```

### Part 4: Strengthen the prompt in `skillMatcher.buildSkillImagePrompt()`

Replace the passive "when relevant, add image_id" with a directive tone. New version:

```
## AVAILABLE UI REFERENCES (pictures the user can see)

CRITICAL: Pictures help elderly users more than any amount of text description. For EVERY guide step that mentions an element listed below, you MUST include "image_id": "<exact-id>" so the user sees a picture of what you're describing. A step that says "click the colorful circle" WITHOUT image_id="chrome-icon" has failed the user.

Available images:
  - "chrome-icon": Chrome browser icon — colorful circle (red, yellow, green, blue)
  - "yahoo-compose-button": Yellow Compose button, upper-left of Yahoo Mail
  ...

Rules:
- Include image_id on every step describing a listed element
- Use the EXACT id string — no variations, no new ids
- If no id matches the element, omit image_id (never invent)
```

---

## Files to Modify

| File | What |
|------|------|
| `server/core/uiReferenceLibrary.js` | Add 8 new entries + promote 5 to `'*'` + update `getIdsForSkill` for wildcard |
| `server/core/skillMatcher.js` | Rewrite `buildSkillImagePrompt()` header to be directive |
| `server/core/agentSdkOrchestrator.js` | Add sticky skill match fallback around line 179 |

`placeholderImageGenerator.js` needs NO change — it iterates the registry and auto-creates placeholders for new entries on next server startup.

---

## Verification

1. **Restart server** — confirm logs show: `[placeholderImageGenerator] Generated 8 placeholder(s)` and `[uiReferenceLibrary] 28/28 references valid`.
2. **Test the same video-call flow** — expected:
   - Turn 1 ("I want to video call my son"): guide steps include `image_id: "chrome-icon"` for "open internet app" and `image_id: "chrome-address-bar"` for "type zoom.us"
   - Turn 3 ("yes its Fred"): sticky match keeps video-call active → agent still has Zoom + browser images available
   - Later: `image_id: "zoom-download-button"` when agent says "click Download"
3. **Manual prompt check** — trigger a `scam-check` query. Confirm the `AVAILABLE UI REFERENCES` section is still injected (because `'*'` images apply) and is shorter (no email/video-call images).
4. **Tests** — `npm test` → all 169 must still pass. No new tests required (this is a data/prompt change, not new logic).
